experiments/programmes/slovene-training-data.md

Slovene training data — a dataset for tokenizers, models and information extraction

open4 experiments2 planned

Can the project assemble, from open sources, a Slovene dataset large and clean enough to train its tokenizers and small language models, and to fine-tune them for information extraction? The project needs this because every later experiment trains or evaluates on it, and the proposal behind the project commits to minimum amounts of text and examples per domain. An answer says which sources the dataset draws on, how much each domain holds once low-quality text is removed, and where examples have to be built rather than found.

MapWhat we now believeThreadsOpenNeedsExperimentsjk sections

Map

What we now believe

  • Open Slovene text is enough to pretrain on in medicine and science, before curation: the survey of open datasets found medicine's new native sources far past the token target ([F2]) and science past both targets on text written in Slovene ([F3]).
  • The curation pipeline cannot yet be trusted with that domain text: what it keeps is clean ([F3]), but every content filter drops mostly good text ([F1]), how well a filter decides swings with the source ([F2]), and the quality filter removes most of the medical source ([F7]).
  • Per-source filter settings win back good text without a measurable rise in bad text: the loosened routes keep about a quarter more good documents than the baseline, with a rise in bad text the draws cannot place above two points ([F12]), and the gain matched its estimate on every route ([F10]). Whether each filter now drops what it targets stays uncalled, since the judge never reached the agreement gate ([F9]).
  • The curated corpus meets every data target once documents carry their own domain: the loosened build clears the corpus, per-domain token and per-domain document targets, and medicine clears the document target only through the medical pages inside the web crawls ([F1]). Under source labels medicine falls short because its one source never held ten thousand distinct texts ([F2]).
  • Medical extraction examples have to be built: almost all of medicine's open documents are translation or machine output ([F1]), and the machine-written sets gather in medicine rather than across the catalogue ([F6]). Medical documents exist in the corpus, but none carries extraction annotation in native Slovene ([F5]).

experiments/programmes/tokenizer-choice-slovenian.md

Which tokenizer should a small Slovene language model use?

open1 experiments6 planned

Slovene is morphologically rich: a noun inflects for six cases in three numbers, and the ending carries case, number and gender. A tokenizer that cuts words into pieces by frequency alone may split stems and endings at arbitrary points. The question is whether a small Slovene model needs a tokenizer changed for this, or whether an existing algorithm is already good enough or best. The project needs the answer before it pretrains its models, since the tokenizer is fixed for the life of a model. An answer names the algorithm and the vocabulary size, rests on metrics shown to measure what they claim, and is checked against the scores of small models trained with the candidates.

MapWhat we now believeThreadsOpenNeedsExperimentsjk sections

Map

What we now believe

  • The morphological gold does not decide which tokenizer looks best, but the set of scored forms does. The stem-ending split of the Sloleks authors and the project's corrected heuristic rank the 24 tokenizers alike [F1]. Scoring only the manually checked forms reorders them, because the manual forms hold fewer nouns and the word classes rank the tokenizers apart [F2]. Every morph score is therefore reported on the manual forms first, and per word class beside the pooled score.
  • Unigram cuts closest to the Sloleks morphemes and is the one algorithm still gaining at 128k, while compression improves for every algorithm. Compression and Morph-Edit-Distance have not levelled off for any of the six algorithms by 128k, and morpheme-boundary F1 still rises there for Unigram alone [F3].

Threads

Trust in the morphological gold

whether the gold that defines a correct morpheme cut changes which tokenizer looks best

F1The heuristic gold and the Sloleks gold rank the tokenizers alike

Open

  • whether metrics beyond boundary F1 separate tokenizers that it ranks alike — answered by morph-metrics-slovenian
  • whether a band from the bootstrap intervals reads the levelling of a metric better than the quarter rule, which turns changes narrower than the interval into falls or gains — answered by morph-metrics-slovenian
  • whether the automatic noun rows of Sloleks 3.2 carry errors that move a ranking, since nouns are the class where the manual and the all-forms rankings agree least — an audit of the lexicon, not yet planned
  • which metrics are redundant — answered by metric-redundancy-slovenian
  • whether the morphological algorithms improve once trained on a correct table — answered by morph-table-slovenian
  • whether a changed BPE training rule helps Slovene — answered by bpe-pruning-slovenian and stem-protection-slovenian
  • whether any tokenizer metric predicts model quality — answered by tokenizer-downstream-slovenian
  • whether freezing the embeddings of some tokens, such as rare tokens or tokens with a single meaning, speeds up pretraining without losing model quality — needs a follow-up on the models of tokenizer-downstream-slovenian, not yet planned

Findings

F1Open Slovene medicine is mostly not written in Slovenekey · H2

Summary

Medicine holds 3.04M open documents, of which 24,757 were written in Slovene; the rest is translation and machine output.

Reading
  • Medicine is the only domain where translated and machine-written documents far outnumber native ones. Everywhere else most documents were written in Slovene. Medicine's total is carried by instruction sets, prompt-and-answer pairs written to train chat models, and by one medical question set translated from English and annotated automatically.
  • Medical examples reach KPI 2 only as machine output. [H2] is refuted as the Statement meant it: open medical documents pass KPI 2's threshold only when machine output counts, and the Statement excludes it. Most of the native remainder is PoVeJMo-VeMo-Med, a corpus of Slovene medical texts the project already downloads, which the clause also excludes.
  • A native medical corpus at scale would overturn it. None turned up in the eight searched source families. Three Hugging Face datasets from the texdata account, gated so they open only on request, are no such candidate. Two are machine-translated from English, and the third is general Slovene web and Wikipedia text ([M7]).
Implication

Medical examples for KPI 2 cannot be collected from open native data. They have to be built, or found beyond the source families this survey searched.

F6Machine-made Slovene is rare in the catalogue and gathers in medicinesupporting F1

Summary

Machine translation touches 15 catalogued datasets and model-written text 9; most wholly synthetic sets are medical.

Reading
  • Most non-native datasets are human translations or bilingual resources, not machine output. Of the rows checked ([M7]), professional translation memories and parallel corpora outnumber machine-translated and synthetic sets together. Five rows the keyword reading flagged turned out to be native Slovene.
  • This qualifies medicine's machine-written majority ([F1]). Machine output is uncommon across the catalogue, but five of the six wholly synthetic sets are medical, and they hold about half of the domain's documents. Medicine's shortfall is a property of that domain's open supply, not of the catalogue as a whole.
  • Native rows misread as native would overturn the proportion. Only rows the keyword reading flagged were checked, so a machine-translated set described without the usual words would still count as native.

runs2a6651164b83452f9dddcb00b72a6038

history2026-09-29 Result drawn as a figure; the table stays under tables/. Lineage rerun at 918a2f0

F2Medicine's new native supply is large in words and small in documentskey · H1 H2

Summary

The four new native medical sources counted by this experiment hold about 7.9M words, thirty times KPI 4, in under four thousand documents.

Reading
  • The national medical journal, Zdravniški vestnik, carries almost all of the new words. Its Slovene articles, sized from a fixed-seed sample ([M6]), hold most of the total, and the Slovene Wikipedia's medicine category most of the rest. The case reports and the guidelines list are small: the reports are few once sentences are grouped, and most guideline links are dead.
  • Native medical text is plentiful and native medical documents are not. [H1] is confirmed: new native text clears KPI 4 many times over, even at the rough two-tokens-per-word estimate ([D6]). [H2] is refuted: native medical documents outside the registry stay under ten thousand under every access filter, and even that count holds the journal three times.
  • Only a different unit of example would overturn it. The one open native medical source left unsized, the CURLICAT corpus, is a collection of sentences with no documents to count. Counting sentences or paragraphs as examples would clear KPI 2 easily; counting documents, nothing in reach adds more than a few thousand.
Implication

Medical pretraining text can be grown from open native sources, so the multilingual fallback is a choice rather than a necessity. Medical information-extraction examples have to be built.

F3Science clears both KPIs on native prose alonekey · H3 H4

Summary

Native science outside the download registry reaches 147,291 open documents and 33.6M estimated tokens, both far past their thresholds.

Reading
  • Science clears both thresholds under the open filter alone. Science here is scientific plus academic datasets, each counted once ([D5]). Loosening access only adds to totals already past both thresholds.
  • Both science clauses hold on native text outside the registry. [H3] and [H4] are confirmed: the totals count only native text outside the download registry, as the clauses require. The margin is wide enough that the rough token estimate ([D6]) cannot change it, and the datasets reporting no size could only raise it.
  • Only the annotated reading of KPI 2 falls short, and it decides no clause. No scientific dataset carries information-extraction annotation, so under that second reading ([D7]) science supplies pretraining text but no ready-made extraction examples.
Implication

Science needs no further sourcing for pretraining. Information-extraction evaluation in the scientific domain has to be built, not found.

F4The catalogue is mostly supply the project does not usesupporting F3

Summary

266 of the 295 catalogued Slovene datasets are outside the download registry.

Reading
  • Nine in ten catalogued datasets are ones the project does not download. The catalogue finds nearly every registry entry; the two it misses are not openly published.
  • This qualifies science clearing both KPIs on native prose ([F3]). Science clears its thresholds on new supply, not only on what is already downloaded, through its new scientific and academic datasets.
  • The headline overstates what matters. Most of the surplus is general-web and miscellaneous text, where every threshold is long cleared. A registry that already held the scientific datasets would undo the qualification.
Implication

The new scientific and academic rows are the shortlist for the next corpus build; the general-web surplus is not worth ingesting.

history2026-09-29 Result drawn as a figure; the table stays under tables/. Lineage rerun at 918a2f0

Verdict

Outcome
refuted
Evidence

Medicine's open documents are machine output ([F1]), and its new native sources hold many words in few documents ([F2]). Science clears both KPIs on native prose the project does not yet download ([F3]), from a catalogue that is mostly such new supply ([F4]).

Discussion
  • Open native Slovene text covers science on both KPIs and medicine on tokens, but not medicine on examples. Medicine has plenty of native words and too few native documents to count as examples.
  • The medical gap was one of documents, not of words. The project's corpus build suggested medicine lacked text. Once the national medical journal and Wikipedia were counted, text was plentiful; what is scarce is many separate native medical documents.
  • The survey measures what is catalogued, not what is written. Sources outside the eight families, and sources whose repositories forbid bulk access, were not counted. A follow-up that builds medical examples inherits the question of which unit counts as an example.
Adoption candidate

Add Zdravniški vestnik and the Wikipedia medicine category to the download registry, with the new scientific and academic rows ([F4]). The pieces to lift are the journal harvester and the Wikipedia category walk in size_medical_sources.py.

Next
  • Build medical information-extraction examples; open supply cannot provide ten thousand native medical documents.
  • Settle why PoVeJMo-VeMo-Med reports far more documents than the corpus build kept, in the curation-quality experiment (curation-quality-slovenian), which tests how much good text the corpus build's filters discard.
  • Decide in a KPI-coverage follow-up whether scientific extraction examples are built or found; none are annotated today.
  • Retry the three gated texdata sets if access is ever granted; the request of 2026-09-22 is unanswered.
  • Size Zdravniški vestnik from a larger sample before ingesting it.
Limitations
  • Under open access, medicine's document total reads unknown by the missing-size rule ([D9]) only because of one sentence collection with no document unit. The verdict reads it as a miss.
  • Tokens are estimated at two per word until the project tokenizer exists.
  • The journal's word count is extrapolated from a sample of about forty articles.
  • Only rows the keyword reading marked non-native were checked against their sources; a native row it misread stays native.
  • The three gated texdata sets are catalogued but unsized; access was never granted.
  • Source families beyond the eight searched were not covered.

Question

Statement

Open-access Slovene text sources, catalogued by domain, size, annotation and document length, contain enough medical and scientific material to meet KPI 2 and KPI 4 without synthetic data.

Rationale

Nobody had written down what Slovene text exists openly beyond what the project already downloads.

  • The project downloads 22 Slovene sources and knows little else. Nobody has recorded what else exists openly, under what licence, in what domain, and whether it is annotated.
  • Earlier survey work left an intuition that medicine is the gap, and no notes. The project's pretraining corpus build, the pipeline that downloads, filters and deduplicates its sources and counts words per source, makes it concrete. Medicine finished at 352 documents and 808,176 words, a hundred times smaller than the next smallest domain.
  • Only a search outside the repo can tell the two readings apart. The gap is either a fact about Slovene or a fact about which sources were picked.
Predictions
Each clause counts openly downloadable Slovene datasets outside the download registry, written in Slovene rather than translated or machine-generated ([D11]), with tokens estimated at two per word ([D6]). An example is one document. Shown as the clause table at the top of the page.
  • Verdict rule: confirmed when H1 to H4 all hold; refuted when any of them falls short under every access filter; inconclusive otherwise.
  • Read beside the clauses, not as clauses: annotated information-extraction examples per domain, the second reading of KPI 2 ([D7]), are reported but decide no clause.

Setup

Inputs

The rows eight searched source families returned for Slovene datasets, and the text this experiment fetched from four native medical sources to size them, described in ## Datasets.

Method / factors

One pass from searched rows to per-domain supply. Nothing is varied; this is a survey.

  • Search the source families and keep every row with the URL it came from ([M1]), then re-read the Hugging Face harvest for rows the first pass missed ([M2]).
  • Merge datasets catalogued twice into one row ([M3]).
  • Size the reachable native medical sources by fetching and counting them ([M6]).
  • Check how the text of every row the keyword reading marks non-native came to exist, and which translation system made it ([M7]).
  • Add token estimates, provenance, registry overlap and KPI fit to every row ([M4]).
  • Total each domain under three access filters and read each total against its KPI ([M5]).
Metrics

Primary estimated tokens per domain against KPI 4; secondary documents per domain, native documents per domain, and annotated examples per domain against KPI 2.

Protocol

A size counts only when read from official statistics or counted over downloaded text ([D6]). A total short of a threshold while datasets report no size is unknown, not a miss ([D9]). Search dates and families are recorded so a refresh knows what to re-check.

Datasets

Survey rows

One row per dataset a searched source family returned, on the catalogue schema ([D4]), kept as JSON per family under data/experiments/data/data-landscape-slovenian/raw/, beside the provenance check of each non-native row ([M7]).

Fetched native medical text

One item per case report, Wikipedia article, journal article or guideline PDF, fetched under data/experiments/data/data-landscape-slovenian/interim/<source>/ for counting only.

Methods

M1Search the source families, one evidence file per familyanalysis.py::load_rows

Input

The eight source families of the language scope ([D1]) and the source list ([D2]). Four agents searched them in parallel on 2026-09-17, one per family.

Output

One JSON file per family under data/experiments/data/data-landscape-slovenian/raw/, each a list of rows on the catalogue schema ([D4]).

How

Nothing is computed here.

  1. Each agent returns, for every row, the URL it read, and leaves a field empty rather than guess.
  2. The rows are kept verbatim as the experiment's evidence, so every later number traces to a row and a URL.
  3. One file per family lets a refresh replace one family without disturbing the others.
  4. The full Hugging Face harvest the agent worked from is kept beside the rows as huggingface-harvest.json.
Code
analysis.py::load_rows
Settings
FAMILY_FILES (which family files are read, in merge order) in analysis.py

M2Re-read the Hugging Face harvest for missed medical and science setsanalysis.py::load_rows

Input

The Hugging Face harvest kept in the evidence of the searched rows ([M1]) and the catalogue as it stood after the first pass.

Output

huggingface-recheck.json, the rows the first pass missed, on the same schema.

How

Two corpora the project already downloads were missing, so the first pass had curated the harvest too tightly.

  1. Re-read the harvest for repositories not already catalogued.
  2. Keep those naming medicine or science in the repository id or its card.
  3. Size each candidate's Slovene configuration through the Hugging Face dataset-viewer size API on 2026-09-19.
  4. Record a repository the API refuses to size as unsized rather than estimated.
Code
analysis.py::load_rows

M3Merge datasets catalogued twice into one rowanalysis.py::merge_duplicates

Input

Every row from the searched rows ([M1]) and the second pass ([M2]), in family order.

Output

One row per dataset, carrying a mirrors field with the addresses of the copies folded into it.

How

The family order puts the publishing repository ahead of any aggregator that mirrors it ([D10]).

  1. Key each row on its dataset name with every non-alphanumeric character dropped.
  2. Keep the first row under a key.
  3. Let a later row under the same key fill only fields the kept row left empty.
  4. Append the later row's URL to mirrors.
Code
analysis.py::merge_duplicates
Settings
FAMILY_FILES (the merge order) in analysis.py

M4Add sizes, provenance, registry overlap and KPI fit to each rowanalysis.py::annotate

Input

The merged rows ([M3]), the download registry configs/data/download.yaml, the corpus build's per-source counts in pretrain/07_statistics/aggregate.json, the counted medical sizes ([M6]) and the provenance checks ([M7]).

Output

Each row gains words_basis, tokens_estimated, provenance, provenance_class, translation_system, in_registry, registry_key, kpi2_fit and kpi4_fit.

How

Each column answers one question the KPIs ask.

  1. Match the row, and every address in mirrors, against the registry's CLARIN handles and Hugging Face repositories. The four corpora fetched by hand match on a fragment of their name.
  2. Take the word count the source reported. Where there is none, take this experiment's own count ([M6]), then the corpus build's count; words_basis says which ([D6]).
  3. Set tokens_estimated to the word count times two, empty when no count exists.
  4. Read provenance from the terms the row's name and notes use ([D11]). Where the row was checked ([M7]), its checked class decides instead, and its translation system is carried over.
  5. Where this experiment counted a source's items itself ([M6]), take that as the row's documents, since it counts in the catalogue's unit.
  6. Set kpi2_fit for medical and scientific rows on 10,000 documents, and kpi4_fit on 500,000 estimated tokens. Either is unknown when its count was never reported ([D9]).
Code
analysis.py::annotate
Settings
TOKENS_PER_WORD (the tokens-per-word estimate), KPI2_EXAMPLES (the KPI 2 threshold), KPI4_TOKENS (the KPI 4 threshold), GENERATED_TERMS (words marking machine output), TRANSLATED_TERMS (words marking translation) in analysis.py

M5Total each domain under three access filters and read it against the KPIsanalysis.py::summarise

Input

The annotated Slovene rows ([M4]). The rows sizing the other-language medical fallback are excluded and written to their own table.

Output

tables/supply-by-domain-and-access.csv, one line per domain and access filter; tables/supply-by-clause.csv, the totals the Predictions are decided on; and the share of each domain written in Slovene as a figure.

How

A row counts toward every domain it carries, so the domain columns do not sum to the catalogue.

  1. For each domain and each access filter ([D8]), total words, estimated tokens, documents, native documents and annotated examples.
  2. Count the datasets behind each total that reported no size.
  3. Read each total against its threshold: cleared is yes, short with nothing missing is no, short with sizes missing is unknown ([D9]).
  4. For medicine and for science, each row counted once, total again over native rows outside the registry only; these decide H1 to H4.
Code
analysis.py::summarise, analysis.py::clause_supply
Settings
DOMAINS (the domain taxonomy), ACCESS_FILTERS (which access classes each filter admits), IE_ANNOTATIONS (annotation types that make a row IE supply) in analysis.py

M6Fetch and count the four reachable native medical sourcessize_medical_sources.py::main

Input

The four native medical rows outside the registry that can be fetched without scraping a repository that forbids bulk access ([D12]). They are the clinical case reports on Hugging Face, the Slovene Wikipedia's medicine category, the Zdravniški vestnik journal and the faculty's clinical guidelines list.

Output

tables/native-medical-sizes.csv, one line per source with items, words, an estimate and its basis. The derived columns ([M4]) read it back as words_basis counted, partial or sampled.

How

Words are whitespace tokens throughout, as in the catalogue.

  1. Case reports: read every row through the Hub rows API. A row is one sentence, so the unit reported is the case report.
  2. Wikipedia: fetch plain-text extracts of every article within two subcategory levels of Kategorija:Medicina.
  3. Zdravniški vestnik: harvest the journal's whole record list through OAI-PMH and keep records whose language is Slovene.
  4. Draw 40 of those with a fixed seed, fetch each PDF at one request per two seconds, and extract its text with pypdf.
  5. Estimate the journal as mean words per counted article times the Slovene record count.
  6. Guidelines: keep the count of guidelines the faculty page states as the item count, and count words over every link that resolves to a PDF. Dead links are left out, so the word count is a lower bound.
  7. On a rerun, reuse the fetched files and recount.
Code
size_medical_sources.py::main
Settings
SAMPLE_SIZE (journal articles drawn), SEED (the draw's seed), WIKI_DEPTH (category levels walked), POLITE_DELAY (seconds between requests to a site) in size_medical_sources.py

M7Check each non-native dataset's source for how its text was madeanalysis.py::provenance_summary

Input

Every catalogue row the keyword reading of provenance ([D11]) did not mark native, with its landing page and mirrors.

Output

provenance-check.json beside the searched rows, one entry per row with its class, source language, translation system, generating model, evidence URL and quote, and a confidence. tables/provenance-by-class.csv and tables/translation-systems.csv total it.

How

Three agents read the sources in parallel on 2026-09-28, each row's landing page first, then the paper or card it cites.

  1. Assign one class: native, human-translated, machine-translated, synthetic (written by a language model), bilingual resource, or mixed.
  2. A bilingual resource is a dictionary, term list or parallel corpus whose translation direction the source does not establish.
  3. A translation post-edited only in part counts as machine-translated.
  4. Record the translation system or generating model only where the source names it, with a verbatim quote; otherwise record it as unknown.
  5. Mark confidence high where the source states it, medium where it is strongly implied, and low where the page could not be read.
  6. Count a mixed row as machine-translated in the systems table only when machine translation is part of its mix.
Code
analysis.py::provenance_summary
Settings
PROVENANCE_OF_CLASS (how each checked class folds into native, translated or generated) in analysis.py

Decisions

D1Survey Slovene in every domain, plus a medical side table for other languages2026-09-14

Decision

Slovene across all domains, with a medical-only side table for other European languages.

Why

The project is Slovene-first, but if open Slovene medicine falls short, the fallback is medical text in a related or larger language. Sizing that fallback costs little while the search is already running.

History
2026-09-14 first version, design interview, question 6

D2Search eight source families, from CLARIN.SI to Slovene medical publishers2026-09-19

Decision

CLARIN.SI, HuggingFace Hub, Zenodo, ELG, LINDAT, OPUS (with parallel medical sets such as EMEA), and Common Crawl derivatives. Also Slovene medical publishers and institutions (Zdravniški vestnik, NIJZ, ZZZS, JAZMP, Wikipedia medical categories), plus synthetic and translated medical sets. Every hit is verified against its landing page.

Why

These are where Slovene text is actually published. Naming them fixes the survey's scope, so the record can say what was covered and a refresh knows what to re-check.

History
2026-09-19 the Hugging Face family was searched a second time [M2]. Two corpora the project already downloads, FinePDFs and Legal-mC4, were missing although the harvest held both. The harvest is now kept as evidence, so a third pass re-reads it instead of re-searching the Hub

D3Catalogue every dataset found, whatever its access2026-09-14

Decision

Every dataset found is a row, regardless of access. An access column (open / login / gated / not downloadable) decides what counts toward the verdict.

Why

A source that exists but is not packaged — a journal archive of individual PDFs, say — is not supply today but is the answer to "what would close the gap". Excluding it would lose the most actionable finding.

History
2026-09-14 first version, design interview, question 20

D4One catalogue row per dataset, one column per question the KPIs ask2026-09-21

Decision

One row per dataset. Its columns are name, source handle or URL, licence, access, languages, domains, reported document count, and reported word or token count. The rest are size verified, annotation type, document-length class, format, already in the download registry, and KPI fit.

Why

Each column answers a question the KPIs ask. Annotation type separates pretraining supply from IE fine-tuning supply; document-length class separates a sentence bank from a document corpus, which matters for pretraining.

History
2026-09-21 registry_key, words_corpus, documents_corpus and words_basis added, so a size taken from the project's own build is distinguishable from one the source reported [D6]

D5Eleven shared domains, with science as scientific plus academic2026-09-14

Decision

Medical, scientific, legal, news, parliamentary, academic, encyclopedic, forum/social, general-web, finance, other. A dataset may carry several. The headline science figure is scientific plus academic.

Why

Shared with the project's other data experiments, so their records can be read against each other.

History
2026-09-14 first version, design interview, question 12

D6Count words, estimate two tokens per word, trust only counted sizes2026-09-22

Decision

Sizes are recorded as the words the source reports, with about 2 subword tokens per word applied for KPI comparisons. A size counts as verified only when read from a downloaded sample or an official statistics page; a publisher's prose claim is unverified.

Why

Published corpus sizes are frequently rounded, stale, or measured differently from what the project would ingest. Marking the provenance of each number keeps an unverified claim from silently becoming a KPI verdict. The token factor stays an estimate until the project tokenizer exists.

History
2026-09-22 a source this experiment fetched and counted itself takes that count ahead of the corpus fallback, marked counted, partial (a lower bound) or sampled (extrapolated from a fixed-seed sample) [M6]

D7Report KPI 2 as documents and as annotated extraction examples2026-09-14

Decision

KPI 2 is reported twice: once as pretraining documents, once as annotated IE examples.

Why

"10k examples" means different things for pretraining and for information extraction, and the proposal commits to both. Reporting one number would hide which commitment is met.

History
2026-09-14 first version, design interview, question 10

D8Report every total under three access filters2026-09-29

Decision

The catalogue CSV and per-domain summary tables under tables/, figures via datachart, produced by analysis.py. Per-domain totals are reported under three access filters: open only, open plus login, and all. No MLflow runs beyond a lineage run logging the catalogue as an artifact.

Why

The three filters are the honest way to state supply: what anyone can download, what a registered researcher can, and what exists at all. A single total would conflate them.

History
2026-09-29 the two access dumbbells and reported-sizes-by-domain removed: no finding rests on them, and the tables carry their numbers

D9Read a shortfall behind unsized datasets as unknown, not a miss2026-09-19

Decision

A domain total that falls short of a KPI threshold while the domain still holds datasets nobody sized is reported as unknown, not as a miss. A total that clears the threshold is yes whatever is missing, since the missing datasets could only raise it. Every table carries the count of datasets behind each verdict that reported no size.

Why

An unreported size is not a verified zero, as the token unit and verification rule holds ([D6]). Reporting a medical domain nobody sized as a KPI 4 miss would turn a gap in the evidence into a finding about Slovene.

History
2026-09-19 first version

D10Keep the publisher's row when a dataset is catalogued twice2026-09-28

Decision

Rows are merged on the dataset name, normalised. The publisher's row wins over an aggregator's row mirroring it. The duplicates only fill fields the winner left empty, and their addresses are kept in a mirrors column.

Why

ELG re-lists CLARIN.SI holdings, so 13 datasets arrived twice and would have been double-counted in every per-domain total. Keeping the publisher's record keeps the licence and size as the publisher states them; the mirrors stay reachable.

History
2026-09-28 Why corrected: every merged duplicate came through ELG; LINDAT's rows matched no CLARIN.SI name

D11Separate native Slovene from translated and machine-made text2026-09-28

Decision

Every row is first read as native, translated or generated from the terms its name and notes use. Every row not read as native is then checked against its card or paper into six classes ([M7]), and the checked class decides. Per-domain totals carry the native document count beside the full one.

Why

The Hypothesis asks whether open sources cover the KPIs without synthetic data, and a document count alone cannot answer that. Medicine forces it: the domain clears KPI 2 only on instruction sets and machine-translated material [F1].

Alternatives
  • Check every row by hand, native ones included — rejected: the non-native rows are where a misreading changes what the Predictions count.
  • Keep the keyword reading alone — rejected: it counted dictionaries and human translation memories as translated text and named no translation system.
History
2026-09-28 non-native rows checked against their sources into six classes, stored as evidence so the reading still reruns ([M7]); five rows moved to native

D12Fetch only medical sources that offer an API or harvesting endpoint2026-09-21

Decision

Sources reachable through an API or a standard harvesting endpoint are fetched whole or sampled. Sources whose repository states there is no bulk export are not fetched. Of the native medical rows, four were fetched and the University of Ljubljana repository was left out.

Why

A word count over downloaded text is the only verification the token unit rule accepts ([D6]), and none of these sources publishes one. Polite per-item fetching is ordinary research use where the publisher offers an endpoint. The one source saying "no bulk export" is left alone.

Alternatives
  • Estimate from document counts alone — rejected: half the rows have none, and the units differ (a case-report row is a sentence).
History
2026-09-21 first version, approved by the project lead before anything was fetched

Findings

F1Every data target clears under document-level labels, and under source labels only the medical examples target misseskey · H1 H2 H3 H4

Summary

Medical documents miss the examples target under source labels and clear it a hundredfold under document labels, while every other count clears under both.

Reading
  • All but four of the fifty-six counts sit above their target, and the four misses are the medical document count under source labels. The misses fall on both builds, with and without the gated sources. Under source labels the medical count is the one medical leaflet source after both dedup stages. Under document labels it is what the TF-IDF classifier that passed the gate ([D3]) assigned medical, mostly from the web crawls ([F3]). The table of every count against its target also reads each target counting one token per word instead of two; no pass changes.
  • [H1], [H2], [H3] and [H4] are each confirmed on the loosened build. The corpus holds over four times the tokens H1 asks for, over three times without the gated sources, and science and medicine each far exceed H2's tokens. Medicine misses the examples target under source labels and clears it under document labels, as H3 predicts; science clears it under both, as H4 predicts. The medical count under document labels stays above its target as long as at least one in a hundred documents labelled medical truly is medical. The gate measured 0.80 off the medical source. The baseline build gives the same four verdicts.
  • A classifier whose precision collapsed on the corpus would overturn the document-label reads. The gate is read on the judged gold, which over-represents dropped text, not on the corpus itself.
Implication

The verdict can be written on the loosened build, since all four bars hold. What remains is where the source-label medical shortfall comes from ([F2]), which decides whether the follow-up is a filter to tune or a dataset to add.

history2026-10-21 first result, from the two classifier passes and the statistics stage of both builds, read on the twelve merged labels ([D2]) with the TF-IDF classifier that passed the gate ([D3])

more tables and figures (1)

F3Medical documents under document labels come almost entirely from the web crawlssupporting F1

Summary

The web crawls supply nineteen in twenty of the documents the classifier labels medical, and the medical leaflet source fewer than one in a hundred.

Reading
  • The medical count is spread over eight web crawls rather than resting on one. The largest single source, the gated culturax crawl, holds about a quarter of the medical documents, and removing all four gated sources leaves three quarters, as the open-source rows of the per-source table show. The medical leaflet source keeps nearly every one of its documents under the medical label, so the classifier agrees with the source label where one exists.
  • This is the mechanism the pass under document labels ([F1]) rests on: the medical examples sit inside general web text, not in a medical dataset. It also means the count's precision is the classifier's precision on web documents, the off-source read the gate measures ([D3]), and not its precision on leaflets, which is near one.
  • Finding that the web documents labelled medical are mostly one site's boilerplate or copies of one leaflet would overturn the reading that these are about a million distinct medical examples. The classifier reads each document's first 2,000 characters alone, and the pass counts documents, not distinct texts.

history2026-10-21 first result, from the two classifier passes

F4The classifier's medical precision holds on the gold documents each final corpus still keepssupporting F1

Summary

On the test gold each final corpus still holds, off-source medical precision stays above its floor on both builds while macro-F1 slips below 0.7.

Reading
  • The documents the corpus keeps are easier for the classifier on medicine and harder on average. The gold was drawn with up to forty kept and forty dropped documents per source and stage, so the test side holds many documents the pipeline removed. Just over half of it survives in the loosened final corpus and about a third in the baseline's. On the survivors, off-source medical precision is 0.82 on the loosened build and 0.85 on the baseline. Macro-F1 falls below its floor on each, by about two hundredths.
  • This supports the medical count under document labels ([F1]) and leaves the gate's verdict as it stands. The gate is read once on the whole test side ([D3]), where the classifier passed. This second read describes the corpus the count was taken on, where the medical precision is at least as high. The lower macro-F1 falls on the other eleven labels, whose counts bear on no target except science. Science's document count is about a hundred times its target, so it holds at any precision above one in a hundred.
  • An off-source medical precision below the floor on the kept documents would overturn the support. The read rests on a few dozen medical assignments off the source, so a handful of mislabels would move it.

F2The medical shortfall under source labels is a source gap, since the medical source never held enough distinct textskey

Summary

The medical source falls below the examples target at exact dedup, which removes only copies, so only a new dataset can close the gap.

Reading
  • Both builds start with more than twice the target and end below it, at different stages. The attribution rule ([M7]) names the first stage after which the medical source holds no more than the target. That is exact dedup on the loosened build and the quality filter on the baseline. The attribution table reads the same without the gated sources, since the medical source is open.
  • [Q1] is partial: each build's shortfall is attributed, but the builds name different stages, so the clause's robustness test, the same cause on both builds, fails. The source's release ships every leaflet twice, as an original and a deduplicated file, and the original repeats a leaflet per medicine. The curation-thresholds experiment traced every medical drop at exact dedup to such a copy. The publisher's deduplicated file holds 5,841 texts, so the source never had ten thousand distinct documents. The rule calls this a curation loss at exact dedup, but that stage removes only copies. The baseline's quality filter does remove medical text, yet the loosened build keeps the source through that filter and still ends below the target. Repairing a filter therefore cannot close the gap, so the cause is a source gap.
  • A medical source with more than ten thousand distinct texts before curation, lost at a filter, would overturn this reading. The loosened build keeps the source through the quality filter, and its distinct texts still fall short.
Implication

Closing the medical examples gap under source labels means adding a dataset, not tuning a filter. The open catalogue datasets in the medical domain show the native ones are small, each medical journal archive under three thousand documents, and the large ones translated or machine-written.

F5Annotated extraction examples exist for science but not for medicine in native Sloveneminor

Summary

The catalogue holds one native science dataset with extraction spans above ten thousand documents and no native medical one above a hundred.

Reading

Read as annotated examples, the examples target holds for science on the native KAS-term dataset alone and for medicine only through the machine-translated HUMADEX dataset, so native medical extraction examples must still be built.

runsno run; analysis.py at 024330f over the landscape catalogue ([M7]).

history2026-10-21 first result, from the landscape catalogue

Verdict

Outcome
confirmed
Evidence

Every count clears its target on the loosened build except medical documents under source labels, which clear under document labels as H3 predicts ([F1]). That shortfall is a source gap: the medical source never held ten thousand distinct texts ([F2]). The medical documents under document labels come from eight web crawls ([F3]), and the classifier's medical precision holds on the gold each final corpus keeps ([F4]).

Discussion
  • Yes, the curated corpus meets all four data targets once each document carries its own domain label. Tokens clear by wide margins under either labelling rule. Only the medical examples target depends on the rule, and it clears only when the web crawls' medical pages are counted.
  • The medical examples sit inside general web text, not in a medical dataset. About a million web documents read as medical, spread over eight crawls, while the one medical source holds under six thousand. The gap rule named exact dedup on the loosened build, a stage that removes only copies, so the rule misreads a source of repeated leaflets.
  • Precision was measured on judged gold, not on the corpus, and sits exactly on its floor. One more mislabelled document would fail it. The gold over-represents dropped text, and the counts are documents, not distinct texts. The margin is wide enough that neither changes a verdict, but a follow-up that needs the medical documents themselves inherits both unknowns.
Adoption candidate

A document-level domain label for the shared corpus, run after the statistics stage. It would carry the classify subcommand of scripts/curate_pretraining_corpus.py, label_corpus and track_corpus_labels with the TF-IDF candidate in slm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py ([M4], [M5]), and the target and gap readings from analysis.py ([M6], [M7]). The lexicon classifier in domains.py and the embeddings candidate failed the gate on the judged gold, whose scores per classifier sit in the gate decision ([D3]), and stay out.

Next
  • Judge a sample of the corpus web documents labelled medical, to measure the classifier's precision on the corpus rather than on the gold ([F1], [F4]).
  • Count medicine in distinct texts rather than documents, inside the medical source (issue #29) and among the web documents ([F3]).
  • Decide whether theses and papers the judge reads as student writing count as science. The classifier puts most theses and open science papers under student, so science under document labels rests on web documents.
  • Build native Slovene medical extraction examples, since the catalogue holds none at scale ([F5]), in the planned medical-ie-slovenian experiment.
  • Make the gap rule tell a stage that removes copies from one that removes text ([F2]).
Limitations
  • Under source labels the medical source counts about three copies per distinct leaflet after conversion ([F2]).
  • The gate is read on the judged gold, which over-represents dropped text, and its medical precision sits exactly on the floor ([D3]).
  • Every count is in documents, not distinct texts, and the classifier reads only each document's first 2,000 characters ([M4]).
  • Tokens are estimated as two per word, never counted with a tokenizer ([M1]).
  • The baseline build is read beside the loosened build, never as the verdict ([D1]).

Question

Builds on

The curation-thresholds experiment, which found that per-source filter settings keep about a quarter more good text than the shared pipeline and left the per-domain volumes of that loosened build untabled. It also answers what the data-landscape survey, which found open native Slovene text covers science on both targets and medicine only on tokens, left open. That survey counted what exists; this experiment reads the corpus the project actually built, and asks whether medical text hidden inside the web crawls changes the medical verdict.

Statement

The curated Slovene corpus meets all four data targets, and medicine clears the examples target only once each document carries its own domain label rather than its source's.

Rationale
  • Every document currently carries its source's domain, so medical text inside the web crawls is invisible. The web crawls hold more than three quarters of the corpus. In the judged sample of the curation-quality experiment, four in a hundred kept web documents were read as medical by the judge, which projects to about a million web documents on the baseline build. Even at a precision of 0.8 that is far past the ten thousand documents the examples target asks for.
  • Under source labels the targets split cleanly. The statistics stage already shows science past both targets and medicine past the token target but far short of the document target on both builds, so only the medical document count can change its verdict.
  • A shortfall has two possible causes that call for different follow-ups. A domain that had the material before curation and lost it points at a filter to tune. A domain that never had it points at the open datasets the landscape survey catalogued, or at building examples.
  • The data can carry the bars, by the counts on disk. Both builds, baseline and loosened, have a finished statistics stage with per-domain documents and words, and clear the corpus-wide and per-domain token targets even with the four gated sources removed. The judged sample holds 637 documents the judge called medical, 196 of them outside the medical source, and the judge agrees with a person on medical-or-not in 142 of 145 hand-labelled documents. The classifier pass over the roughly 41 million documents of the loosened build is one tracked run of a few CPU hours. Counts in the per-domain totals of both builds and the judged gold per domain.
Predictions
Every clause is read on the final corpus of the validated build ([D1]), with a token counted as a word times two, a document as one example, and a domain assigned by source label or by the document-level classifier ([D2]); a pass is a total above its target. Shown as the clause table at the top of the page.
  • Verdict rule: confirmed when all four bars hold; refuted when any bar is refuted; inconclusive when the classifier fails its quality gate ([D3]) so that H3 and H4 cannot be read under document labels. Q1 is read beside that outcome and does not change it.
  • Read beside the clauses, not as clauses: the classifier's macro-F1 and per-domain precision on the judged gold; the second reading of the examples target, annotated extraction examples per domain from the landscape catalogue; the same per-domain totals on the baseline build.

Setup

Inputs

The loosened and the baseline corpus builds with their statistics stage, the judged sample of the curation-quality experiment as domain gold, and the landscape survey's catalogue of open Slovene datasets. All four are read in place from the earlier experiments and described in ## Datasets.

Method / factors

One pass from source-labelled counts to a per-target verdict.

  • Count documents and words per domain and source at every curation stage of both builds, from the statistics stage and the stage folders ([M1]).
  • Score every document against one lexicon per domain and assign the highest-scoring domain when it clears a threshold and leads the runner-up by a margin, else the source's own label ([M2]).
  • Measure that classifier on the judged gold, macro-F1 over the twelve scored labels and precision per domain, and pass or fail the gate ([M3]).
  • Where it fails, fit a supervised classifier on the tune side and read the same gate ([M4]).
  • Label every document of the final corpus of both builds and total documents and tokens per domain under the document-level labels ([M5]).
  • Read each target under each counting rule, source versus document labels, all sources versus gated removed, and write the pass/fail table ([M6]).
  • Attribute each shortfall to the stage that lost the material or to a missing source, and list the catalogue datasets that would close it ([M7]).
  • Factors: the labelling rule (source label, document-level classifier); the source set (all, gated removed); the build (loosened, baseline).
Metrics

Primary pass or fail per target and counting rule; secondary macro-F1 and medical precision of the classifier on the judged gold, estimated tokens and documents per domain — each defined in experiments/GLOSSARY.md.

Protocol

The classifier pass over a full build is a tracked run, one per build, with per-domain totals logged to MLflow. The counts, the pass/fail table, the gap attribution and the catalogue join are recomputed by analysis.py from the statistics files and the run outputs.

Datasets

Loosened build

The curated corpus the curation-thresholds experiment rebuilt with its per-route loosened filter settings, read in place from that experiment's data folder (pretrain-loosened/). One item is one document of the final stage, after both dedup stages. It holds 18 Slovene sources and about 41 million documents. Its last three stages, the two dedup stages and the statistics, were built 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-19 at commit 8e21f67; the earlier stages are reused from that experiment's candidate builds of 2026-10-05 onward.

Baseline build

The shared pretraining corpus under data/pretrain/, built by the pipeline on main from the same 18 sources. It holds about 30 million final-stage documents, built 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-08 at commit 2ece205. Its rows sit in the same table as the loosened build's.

Judged gold

The 8,930 documents of the curation-quality experiment's judged sample, each joined on its id to the domain its judge assigned. The sample was drawn in September from an earlier build, up to 40 kept and 40 dropped documents per source, stage and decision, so it over-represents dropped text and small sources. It spans 20 sources, two of them (parlamint_si, legal_mc4) in neither build here. Its kept flag is the drawn stage's decision then, not membership in either final corpus. About half the documents were cut to 2,000 characters before judging. Sample and verdicts are hash-checked, then halved into a tune and a test side ([D3]) under final/gold-tune-test-split/. The judged gold per judge domain,

more tables and figures (1)

Landscape catalogue

The data-landscape survey's 295 rows for Slovene, one per dataset with its domains, access, size and annotation, searched 2026-09-17. A dataset listing several domains counts once under each, and the survey's domain names are renamed to the judge's labels ([D2]).

Methods

M1Count each source's documents after every curation stage of both buildsanalysis.py::funnel_source_rows

Input

Each build's curation output folder. One item is one source at one stage, such as kas after the quality filter, with the documents that stage read and wrote. The counts come from the small completion file each per-source stage writes beside its output, from the exact-dedup stage's own files, and from the statistics stage's file per source.

Output

One row per build and source in tables/funnel-documents-by-source.csv. It carries the source's domain label and access from the dataset registry, its documents after each of the seven stages, its final words, estimated tokens and the share of its documents kept. The same counts summed over the sources sharing a domain label, with how many sources each sum spans, are in tables/funnel-documents-by-domain.csv, which Q1 and [M7] read.

How

Documents are counted at every stage; words only at the last, since counting them at every stage means splitting every stage's text into words again.

  1. For the five stages that run per source (convert, language, spam, quality, repetition), read each source's documents read and written from its completion file. Stop if a stage read other than what the stage before it wrote, the sign of a stage reused from another build.
  2. Exact dedup runs over the whole corpus and records no per-source count, so count the documents in each source's files once. Cache the counts under this experiment's interim/ with the stage's document digest, a hash of its output, and reuse them while the digest holds.
  3. Take each source's documents and words after sentence dedup from the statistics stage; a source it has no file for lost its last document earlier and counts zero there. Its words leave out stopwords and punctuation. Estimate tokens as t=2w, where w is that word count, the conversion every KPI reading in the project uses.
  4. Stop unless the per-source sums equal the counts both dedup stages recorded for the whole corpus.
  5. Compute the share kept, r=nfinal/nconvert, where nconvert is the source's documents after conversion and nfinal after sentence dedup. Sum every count per build and domain label, and recompute r on the sums.
Code
analysis.py::funnel_source_rows, summed by analysis.py::funnel_domain_rows
Settings
none; the stages counted are the pipeline's own

M2Label each document with the domain its own words point toslm4ie/data/curate/inspect/domains.py::label_document

Input

One document of a corpus build, its text and its source's domain label. The thirteen marker-word lists, one per judge label ([D2]), hand-curated in configs/classifier-lexicon.yaml. An entry is a whole word (dne) or a prefix ending in * (zdravil*), which matches every word starting with it, since Slovene inflects heavily. Each entry sits in a tier, strong for words that almost only occur in that domain and weak for words common there but seen elsewhere too. The lists were seeded from the words most distinctive of each judge domain on the tune half of the gold, ranked by log-odds against the other domains, in the seed table. They were then pruned by hand to words that name the domain's subject or genre, dropping words that mark one source or one text, so the gate measures the domain and not the source.

Output

One label of the thirteen per document.

How
  1. Split the text into words, runs of letters and digits, lowercased. Let n be their count.
  2. For every word and every domain, take the weight of the strongest entry of that domain the word matches, ws=3 for a strong entry, ww=1 for a weak one, zero when none matches. Sum over the words into hd, the weighted hits of domain d.
  3. Score each domain as hits per thousand words, sd=1000hd/n; an empty text scores zero everywhere.
  4. Rank the domains by score, ties towards the earlier list. Assign the leader when the text has at least m words, s(1)≥τ and s(1)−s(2)≥μ, where s(1) and s(2) are the leading and runner-up scores, τ the threshold and μ the margin. The length floor m stops one strong word deciding a short text on its own.
  5. Otherwise keep the source's label, mapped through the fallback table when it is not one of the thirteen; the mixed-genre reference corpus falls back to other.
Code
slm4ie/data/curate/inspect/domains.py::label_document
Settings
rule.threshold (τ, the lowest leading score that assigns a domain), rule.margin (μ, the smallest lead over the runner-up), rule.min_words (m, the shortest text the rule is read on), weights (the hit weight of each tier), fallback (source labels outside the thirteen and the label they count as), lexicons (the entries per domain and tier). Threshold and margin are picked on the tune half of the gold ([D3], [M3]).

M3Score the lexicon classifier on the judged gold and read its gateanalysis.py::score_gold

Input

The judged gold, halved into its tune and test side ([D3]). One item is one judged document with its text, the judge's domain and its source's label. The lexicons and the length floor of [M2].

Output

Four tables. The tune-side grid: one row per threshold and margin pair with its macro-F1 and medical precision, the pick marked. The gate: one row per side with its documents, the rule read, macro-F1 and medical precision, the same precision and recall over the documents of other sources, and whether both floors hold. Only the test row is the gate; the tune row shows the fit. Precision, recall and F1 per domain and side, each also read off the domain's own source. The confusion counts: documents per judge domain and assigned label, per side.

How
  1. Score every judged document once against the lexicons ([M2], steps 1 to 3), so every rule reads the same scores. Labels are read with scientific and academic folded into science ([D2]).
  2. On the tune side, read the rule ([M2], step 4) at every threshold τ∈{0,5,…,100} and margin μ∈{0,5,…,40}, the length floor fixed at the config's m. For each label d, let gd be its gold documents, ad the documents assigned it and cd those that are both. Precision is Pd=cd/ad, recall Rd=cd/gd and Fd=2PdRd/(Pd+Rd), zero where undefined. Macro-F1 is the mean of Fd over the twelve labels, each counting once.
  3. Pick the pair with the highest macro-F1 at four decimals; ties go to the higher medical precision, then the lower threshold, then the lower margin. The pick is written into the config; the analysis stops when the config's rule differs from it.
  4. On the test side, read the config's rule and compute the same metrics. The gate holds when macro-F1 is at least 0.7 and medical precision off the medical source, step 5, at least 0.8 ([D3]). A hash of the lexicons is frozen at that read; a changed lexicon stops the analysis, so the test side is read once per lexicon.
  5. Read each domain's precision and recall again on the documents whose fallback label is not that domain, where only the lexicons can assign it. H3 rests on this read: the medical source's leaflets keep their label without any classifier.
Code
analysis.py::score_gold (step 1), analysis.py::rule_grid_rows and analysis.py::check_rule_tuned (steps 2 and 3), analysis.py::gate_rows and analysis.py::check_lexicons_frozen (step 4), analysis.py::gate_domain_rows and analysis.py::confusion_rows (step 5 and the per-domain tables), all over analysis.py::label_metrics
Settings
in analysis.py, GRID_THRESHOLDS (the thresholds searched), GRID_MARGINS (the margins searched), GATE_MACRO_F1 (the macro-F1 floor of [D3]), GATE_PRECISION (the precision floor of [D3]), GATE_DOMAIN (the domain the precision floor reads, medical), LABEL_MERGE (the judge labels folded into one, scientific and academic into science), DECIMALS (the rounding of every metric, and of the pick); in configs/classifier-lexicon.yaml, rule.min_words (the length floor, fixed before the search), rule.threshold (the picked threshold) and rule.margin (the picked margin)

M4Fit a supervised classifier on the tune side and read the same gateslm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py::fit_classifier

Input

The tune side of the judged gold ([D3]); one item is one judged document's text and judge domain. The test side is read once per candidate. Two candidates in configs/classifier-supervised.yaml, each a logistic regression over the twelve scored labels ([D2]) with its own features. tfidf uses word and character n-grams weighted by TF-IDF, a term's count in the document discounted by how many documents carry it. embeddings uses one vector per document from the multilingual-e5-small sentence encoder, which reads the first 512 tokens.

Output

Per candidate, the gate, per-domain and confusion tables of [M3] under tables/classifier-<candidate>-…. For tfidf: gate, per domain, confusion. For embeddings: gate, per domain, confusion. The regularisation grid: tfidf and embeddings. The fit itself is kept under final/classifier-supervised/.

How
  1. Cut every text to its first 2,000 characters, the length the gold was cut to before judging, so the gate measures the classifier on the text it will read in the corpus.
  2. Split the tune side into k stratified folds that keep copies of one text together. For each regularisation strength C in the config's list, fit the features and a logistic regression inside each fold, every class weighted to the same total, and score the out-of-fold predictions by the macro-F1 of [M3]. Pick the highest, ties to the smaller C, the stronger regularisation. Refit the pick on the whole tune side and save it.
  3. Label both sides with the saved fit and read the gate of [M3], steps 4 and 5. A document's fallback label still comes from its source, so the off-source read is the same read.
  4. Reuse a saved fit while the config, the tune documents and the library version hash to what it was fitted from; a change stops the analysis, so each candidate's test side is read once.
Code
slm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py::fit_classifier (steps 1 and 2), analysis.py::fit_or_load_candidate (step 4), analysis.py::write_gate_tables with analysis.py::label_predicted (step 3), over the texts of analysis.py::gold_texts
Settings
max_chars (characters read per text), regularisation (the C values tried), folds (k), workers (folds fitted at once), seed (the fold assignment), max_iterations (solver iterations before a fit is declared not converged); per candidate features (tfidf or embeddings), for tfidf word_ngrams (shortest and longest word n-gram), char_ngrams (shortest and longest character n-gram), min_df (documents an n-gram must occur in), max_features (n-grams kept per kind); for embeddings model (the encoder), revision (the hub commit loaded), prefix (text the encoder expects before each document), batch_size (documents encoded at once), max_length (tokens read per document); in analysis.py, SUPERVISED_CANDIDATES (the candidates read, in order)

M5Label every final-corpus document of both builds with the passing classifierslm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py::label_corpus

Input

The final stage of one build, after both dedup stages ([D1]); one item is one document, its text and its source. The tfidf fit of [M4] that passed the gate, saved under final/classifier-supervised/tfidf.pkl. The ids of the judged gold.

Output

Per build, one JSON file under final/ with the documents and words per source and assigned label, and the gold ids the build still holds, read by [M6] and [M7]. The same totals summed over sources, documents and words per label, are logged as one MLflow run per build.

How
  1. Read every shard of the stage, one process per shard, and label each document with the saved fit, which reads its first 2,000 characters ([M4], step 1).
  2. Count each document under its source and its assigned label. Count its words as the statistics stage counts them, word tokens with at least one letter and two characters, stopwords left out, so tokens estimated as t=2w match [M1].
  3. Note every gold id the stage still holds, so a gold document's true kept flag is known for this build.
  4. Sum the shards and stop unless the documents counted equal those the stage's completion record holds, so no shard is missed. Each finished shard is saved as it ends, so a pass that stops part way resumes from where it was. It resumes only while the stage, fit, stopwords and gold ids are the ones it started with.
Code
slm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py::label_corpus (steps 1 to 4), slm4ie/data/curate/inspect/supervised.py::track_corpus_labels (the JSON and the MLflow run, with the hashes of the fit and the gold file), run by scripts/curate_pretraining_corpus.py classify
Settings
on the command line, --classifier (the saved fit), --gold (the judged sample whose ids are looked for), --checkpoint (the file of finished shards), --max-workers (shards read at once), --shards-per-source (the first shards read per source, for a smoke run only); in the build's curation config, stopwords (the words left out of every word count)

M6Read every target under every counting rule on both buildsanalysis.py::read_corpus_labels

Input

The two files of [M5], one per build, with documents and words per source and assigned label. The per-source funnel of [M1], to check them against. Each source's domain label and access from the dataset registry. The gate verdict of [M3] and [M4].

Output

the target table, one row per build, domain, measure, labelling rule and source set. Each row holds the count, the target and whether the count is above it. It also holds the share of the count that must truly belong to the domain for it to stay above. The totals behind it: documents and estimated tokens per domain under each labelling rule, with the open sources beside, and the same per source and assigned label. The gate read again on the test-side gold documents each final corpus still holds.

How
  1. Stop unless the saved fit hashes to what both corpus passes logged, and unless every source's documents and words in a pass equal what the statistics stage counted for it.
  2. Sum documents and words per domain under each labelling rule. Under source labels a document counts under its source's registry label; under document labels, under the label the classifier assigned it. Scientific and academic both count as science ([D2]). Sum once with every source and once without the four gated ones.
  3. Read the corpus in estimated tokens t=2w, where w is its word count, and in words, each word read as one token, against 5×109. Read science and medicine in estimated tokens and in words against 5×105, and in documents against 104.
  4. A count passes when it is above its target. A count under document labels is not read when the classifier that labelled the corpus failed its gate ([D3]).
  5. For each count n with target T, the share needed is T/n: the lowest precision at which the domain's true documents or tokens would still clear the target.
  6. Read the gate's macro-F1 and medical precision of [M3] again on the test-side documents whose ids [M5] found in each final corpus, beside the gate and never as it.
Code
analysis.py::read_corpus_labels (step 1), analysis.py::domain_totals (step 2), analysis.py::kpi_rows with analysis.py::kpi_row (steps 3 to 5), analysis.py::final_corpus_gate_rows (step 6)
Settings
in analysis.py, CORPUS_TOKEN_TARGET (estimated tokens the corpus must hold), DOMAIN_TOKEN_TARGET (estimated tokens per domain), DOMAIN_DOCUMENT_TARGET (documents per domain), TARGET_DOMAINS (the domains read, science and medical), TOKENS_PER_WORD (the word-to-token estimate), CORPUS_CLASSIFIER (the candidate whose fit labelled the corpora), CORPUS_CLASSIFIER_SHA256 (the hash of that fit both passes logged)

M7Attribute each missed target to a missing source or to the stage that lost itanalysis.py::gap_rows

Input

The rows of [M6] whose count is not above its target. The per-source funnel of [M1], documents after every stage of both builds. The landscape catalogue.

Output

the attribution, one row per missed target with the documents its sources held after conversion and at the end, the cause and the stage named. The open catalogue datasets of each domain with a missed target that the corpus does not yet hold. The catalogue datasets annotated with extraction spans per domain, the second reading of the examples target.

How
  1. Sum, per stage, the documents of the sources whose label folds into the missed domain, leaving out the gated sources where the row does.
  2. If the sources held no more than the target after conversion, the cause is a source gap. Otherwise it is a curation loss, and the stage named is the first after which they hold no more than the target.
  3. A missed target under document labels or in words names no cause, since those counts exist only at the final stage.
  4. List the catalogue datasets of each missed domain that are openly downloadable and not in the dataset registry, largest first. Catalogue domains are renamed to the judge's labels, science folded ([D2]).
  5. List, per domain, the catalogue datasets annotated with extraction spans, whatever their access.
Code
analysis.py::gap_rows with analysis.py::domain_stage_counts (steps 1 to 3), analysis.py::gap_catalogue_rows (step 4), analysis.py::ie_example_rows (step 5)
Settings
in analysis.py, IE_ANNOTATION (the catalogue's annotation value for extraction spans), CATALOGUE_DOMAINS (the catalogue's domain names renamed to the judge's labels)

Decisions

D1Read the targets on the loosened build, with the baseline beside it2026-10-20

Decision

The validated corpus is the final stage of the loosened build the curation-thresholds experiment named its adoption candidate, as it stands in that experiment's data folder. The baseline build on the shared path is tabled beside it under every counting rule, never as the verdict.

Why

The loosened settings are the ones the shared corpus will carry once adopted, so a verdict on the baseline would be stale on arrival. The baseline beside it shows what the filter change gained per domain.

Alternatives
  • Wait for the shared corpus to be rebuilt with the loosened settings — the same documents, weeks later.
  • Read the baseline alone — answers a question about a build the project is leaving behind.
History
2026-10-20 set at record creation; the issue's ordering comment asked the verdicts to wait for frozen thresholds, which the loosened build now carries.

D2The judge's document-level domains are the gold, and its labels, science merged, are the label set2026-10-20

Decision

The classifier predicts the curation-quality judge's domain labels: medical, scientific, legal, news, parliamentary, academic, wiki, forum, blog, student, web, finance, other. Scientific and academic are folded into one label, science, so twelve are scored and labelled. Scored on the judge's 8,930 documents. The issue's names map onto these as encyclopedic = wiki, forum/social = forum, general-web = web.

Why

It is the only document-level domain gold that exists, it spans every source, and the judge agrees with a person on medical-or-not in 142 of 145 hand-labelled documents. A label set that differs from the gold's cannot be scored on it.

Alternatives
  • Source labels as gold — blind to exactly the web documents the classifier exists to find.
  • A fresh hand-labelled set — days of labelling for a question the judge's labels already answer on medicine.
History
2026-10-20 scientific and academic folded into science for scoring and labelling, at the code phase: both are science writing, the judge's line between them was every classifier's largest confusion in [M3] and [M4], and the headline already summed them. The lexicon rule still reads its margin on the two scores before the fold; folding them first would move its test macro-F1 by 0.0002.

D3The classifier must pass a quality gate on the gold before any count under document labels is read2026-10-21

Decision

The judged gold is halved under a fixed seed into a tune and a test side, copies of one text together and each domain split evenly. Settings are picked on the tune side. A classifier passes with test macro-F1 at least 0.7 and off-source medical precision at least 0.8. Failing that, a supervised classifier is tried the same way.

Why

A classifier that mislabels one web page in five would clear the ten thousand bar on noise alone. A gate read on the tuning documents measures fit, not that error rate. The gold holds dozens of groups of copied text, which a random split would put on both sides. The gate decides whether a clause can be read, never how.

History
2026-10-21 at conclusion, two departures from the issue's requirement 4 recorded: the medical floor reads precision rather than F1, since H3 counts what the classifier assigns medical; the topic-model baseline it named for escalation was not found on this machine, so the supervised candidates were read without it.

Reproduce

Every run logs to the project's MLflow server under slm4ie/data/kpi-coverage-slovenian. Data lives under data/, a symlink to /vault/data/SLM4IE/. Both corpus builds must be in place: the baseline under data/pretrain/ and the loosened build under the curation-thresholds experiment's interim/pretrain-loosened/. The curation-quality experiment's judged sample and verdicts, and the data-landscape survey's catalogue, are read in place. The gold split, the lexicon freeze and the supervised fits under final/ are frozen; deleting one is a deliberate second read of the test side.

Curation pipeline quality — Slovenian

in Slovene training dataPR #11concluded 2026-09-30
Hypothesis
The eight-stage curation pipeline removes low-quality records without discarding valid domain-specific text; each stage's drop rate is explained by its intended filter, not by domain or source artefacts.
refuted
