history2026-10-19 first result, from the third draw ([D13], [D16])

Verdict

Outcome
inconclusive
Evidence

A clause read on a judge run below the agreement gate counts as neither confirmed nor refuted ([D3]). Ignoring the gate, the fresh draw would refute every clause, with failing rates outnumbering holding ones on each. The loosened build keeps about a quarter more good documents than the baseline, and the interval on its rise in bad text spans the bar ([F12]). Its gain in good text matches the per-route estimate within two percent on every route ([F10]).

Discussion
  • Whether each filter now drops what it targets cannot be told, but the loosened settings keep a quarter more good text. No clause is called, since every judge run sits below the agreement gate ([F9]). The amended question ([D17]) is answered yes ([F12]), and the gain landed where the per-route estimate put it ([F10]).
  • Simple rules cannot remove all bad text. Once the rules that misread Slovene prose were repaired or switched off ([D8], [D9]), no letter, stopword or line measure tested separated the remaining web junk from good text. Every further cut lost one good document per bad one. What the rules leave is boilerplate and link lists made of ordinary words.
  • The judge, not the filters, limited what could be measured. Agreement with the person fell from 0.51 to 0.39 between two runs of the same model, rubric and labelled documents.
  • Forty judged kept documents per source cannot bound the bad text. The three builds were judged in separate runs, so judge drift and setting changes are confounded. A follow-up judges the baseline and the new corpus in one run, and tests a learned classifier for the junk the rules cannot see ([D14]).
Adoption candidate

Carry the loosened route settings into the shared corpus: the three routes and per-source settings of configs/curation-routes-loosened.yaml move into configs/data/curate.yaml, with the repaired letter rule on ([M2]). Already in slm4ie/: the route machinery, the letter-rule filter, a sentence-dedup guard that skips sentences past datatrove's 16-bit index, and a sampler fix that makes its index lookups fast. Code to promote from analysis.py: the precision, trade-off and residual-rate functions ([M3], [M8], [M12]). The quality and dedup stages' modules changed, so the shared corpus rebuilds from the quality stage on at merge.

Next
  • Judge the baseline's and the new corpus's kept documents in one run, over forty per source, to bound the rise in bad text ([F12]).
  • Test a quality classifier trained on the judge's verdicts ([D14]), in the planned quality-classifier-slovenian experiment.
  • Decide whether the news source's one-line teasers need a length floor ([F8]).
  • Catch documents with a punctuation mark after every word, such as two theses and one PDF the repetition filter used to drop.
  • Check whether the repetition target fits what its rules catch ([F11]).
  • Fix the medical source's extraction (issue #29, [F6]).
  • Add per-domain counts once the KPI coverage classifier exists ([D4]).
Limitations
  • Every judged number rests on a run below the gate ([F9]).
  • The three builds were judged in separate runs, the baseline's on the earlier audit's draw.
  • About forty judged kept documents per source leave the rise's interval ten points wide ([F12]).
  • Kept is read before the dedup stages.
  • The loosened build's tokens per domain were not tabled; it only loosens filters.
  • The third draw covers only changed filters and sources ([D13]), so the language and spam clauses rest on the fresh draw, which became tuning evidence.
  • The amended bar's interval rule came after its point estimate was seen ([D17]).
  • The medical source's count is about three times its distinct texts ([F6]).

Question

Builds on

The curation-quality experiment (curation-quality-slovenian) found that every content filter drops mostly text worth keeping. It also found that how well a filter decides swings with the source. It measured the pipeline without changing it, and left the repair to this experiment.

Statement

Once each source takes its own route through the content filters, with retuned thresholds, each filter mostly drops the text it is built to catch. The spam, quality and repetition filters then also mostly drop bad text, on a fresh draw held back from tuning.

Rationale

The earlier audit points to settings, not to the filters themselves.

  • The filters sort in the right direction. In the earlier audit, kept text beat dropped text at every content filter when the judge compared them in pairs. The filters are miscalibrated, not inverted.
  • Their failures sit on particular sources. The spam filter drops mostly real spam on the raw web crawls and mostly clean prose on curated sources. The quality and repetition filters decide at about a coin flip on the medical and academic sources.
  • The causes are known and fixable. Parliamentary rebuttals hit a spam term, and patient leaflets repeat dosage lines by design. Gopher's thresholds were tuned on English web text, not on Slovene curated prose.
Predictions
Every clause is read on the fresh draw, judged only after the thresholds are frozen. A rate is read pooled over sources, and on each source the filter still runs on with at least 20 judged drops. Each filter is judged on its own target ([D1]): the language filter on non-Slovene text, the spam filter on spam, the quality filter on ill-formed text, the repetition filter on repeated furniture. Shown as the clause table at the top of the page.
  • Verdict rule: confirmed when all five clauses hold; refuted when any clause is refuted; inconclusive otherwise.
  • Read beside the clauses, not as clauses: the share of bad text among kept documents per stage; retention per source, with the medical, scientific, legal and parliamentary sources called out; the corpus total against KPI 3 and the medicine and science totals against KPI 4 ([D4]); per-domain counts at every stage from the document-level domain classifier of the planned KPI coverage experiment, once it exists.

Setup

Inputs

The curated corpus rebuilt under each candidate route, the earlier audit's judged sample and hand labels for tuning, and a fresh draw for validation, described in ## Datasets.

Method / factors

One tuning pass on old evidence, one validation pass on new evidence.

  • Restate the earlier audit's per-source baseline from the rebuilt corpus, since five sources were counted twice there.
  • Give each source one of three routes through the content filters, a starting point taken from the earlier audit's per-source numbers.
  • Tune the thresholds of each route against the earlier judge verdicts and hand labels.
  • Freeze the thresholds, rebuild the corpus, and draw a fresh sample under a new seed.
  • Judge the fresh draw with the earlier rubric.
  • Factors: the route each source takes, the Gopher quality and repetition floors, the language-identification threshold, and the spam thresholds on the repaired spam signal. The dedup stages stay fixed.
Metrics

Primary target precision per content filter and source, and drop precision at the lenient bar for the spam, quality and repetition filters. Secondary: residual bad rate, retention per source, corpus and domain totals in estimated tokens, and Cohen's κ between the judge and the person. Each metric is defined in experiments/GLOSSARY.md.

Protocol

Analysis-only for the judging: analysis.py recomputes every table from the corpus counts and the verdict files. Each corpus rebuild logs to MLflow: the baseline under slm4ie/data/curate, since it is the shared corpus, and each candidate build under slm4ie/data/curation-thresholds-slovenian. Findings rest on one judge run, and its agreement with the hand labels is read on that same run ([D3]).

Datasets

Baseline corpus

The shared pretraining corpus rebuilt with the pipeline as it stands on main ([D5], the baseline build), one row per source with its domain, kind, licence and size before and after curation. Built 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-08 at commit 2ece205 from 18 Slovene sources.

Candidate-routes build

The same 18 sources rebuilt with every source on its route ([M1]) and the letter rule repaired ([M2]), in this experiment's own data folder ([D6]). The second candidate of the tuning pass, with the curated-prose quality settings of [D9], built 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-14 at commit 4425f23. It replaced the first candidate, built 2026-10-08 to 2026-10-11 at commit a03f2dd from the baseline's converted documents, whose counts stay in MLflow.

Loosened build

The same 18 sources rebuilt with the per-route loosened settings ([D16]) into a folder of its own beside the frozen build ([D13]), built 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-19 at commit 8e21f67.

Fresh draw

Kept and dropped documents of the frozen build, 40 per source, stage and decision under seed 20261014 ([D10]), each cut to its opening 2,000 characters for the judge. Its one judge run also holds the earlier audit's 116 hand-labelled documents ([D11]); the verdicts sit under interim/.

Third draw

Kept and dropped documents of the loosened build at the quality and repetition filters, 40 per source and decision under seed 20261019 ([D13]), with the same hand-labelled documents in its judge run.

Methods

M1Send each source through one of three routes of filter settingsslm4ie/data/curate/config.py::resolve_profiles

Input

The 18 selected Slovene sources, each a set of documents converted from its extracted text. One item is a source with its name, such as gigafida.

Output

Per source, the settings each content filter applies to its documents. They drive the language, spam, quality and repetition filters of every candidate build.

How

A route is a named set of content-filter settings that every source of one kind shares.

  1. Assign each source to a route by how the earlier audit's filters fared on it. Seven web crawls take the raw-crawl route. Seven edited-text sources (wiki, legal, reference corpus, parliament, news, student essays, and the crawl of PDF documents) take the curated-prose route. The four medical and academic sources take the medical-and-academic route.
  2. Start from the shared pipeline's settings, with the quality filter's letter rule counting only tokens that are not punctuation ([M2]). The raw-crawl route changes nothing else.
  3. On the curated-prose route, switch the language and spam filters off and widen every repetition limit by half. Lower the letter floor of the quality filter from 0.8 to 0.55 ([D9]).
  4. On the medical-and-academic route, switch the spam filter off and keep the language filter. Widen the repetition limits by half, and double the limits on repeated lines.
  5. Merge a source's own settings over its route's. The news source skips the rule on lines ending in an ellipsis ([D9]). The PDF crawl keeps the language filter on.
  6. For the loosened build, in its own folder, apply the per-route changes chosen on the judged samples ([D16]).
Code
slm4ie/data/curate/config.py::resolve_profiles
Settings
profiles (the three routes, each a set of filter settings), overrides (the route each source takes, and its own settings on top), max_non_alpha_words_ratio (minimum share of words containing a letter), max_ellipsis_lines_ratio (maximum share of lines ending in an ellipsis; 0 switches the rule off), min_doc_words (fewest words a document may have), min_stop_words (fewest stopwords a document must contain; 0 switches the rule off), dup_line_frac (maximum share of lines repeated in the document), top_n_grams (maximum share of characters covered by the most frequent word pair, triple and quadruple), dup_n_grams (maximum share of characters inside repeated 5- to 10-word sequences; an empty list switches the rule off), enabled (whether a filter runs on the source at all); in configs/curation-routes.yaml, and for the loosened build in configs/curation-routes-loosened.yaml

M2Count only words, not punctuation marks, in the quality filter's letter ruleslm4ie/data/curate/stages/quality.py::LetterShareGopherQualityFilter

Input

One document reaching the quality filter, as plain text. The filter's settings come from the document's route ([M1]).

Output

The document kept or dropped, with the first rule it failed. Kept documents go on to the repetition filter.

How

The quality filter applies the Gopher heuristics, rule-based checks published with DeepMind's Gopher model. One of them requires most words to contain a letter, which is meant to catch tables of numbers and symbol junk.

  1. Split the text into tokens with datatrove's Slovene word splitter, which makes every punctuation mark its own token.
  2. Set aside the tokens made only of punctuation. The length and word-length rules already read only the remaining tokens.
  3. Apply every other Gopher rule unchanged, in datatrove's order.
  4. Compute the letter share over the remaining tokens, s=a/w, where w is the number of tokens that are not pure punctuation and a is how many of them contain a letter. Drop the document when s is below the floor.
Code
slm4ie/data/curate/stages/quality.py::LetterShareGopherQualityFilter
Settings
max_non_alpha_words_ratio (despite its name, the floor on the letter share, 0.8), alpha_words_skip_punctuation (whether punctuation tokens are set aside before the letter share is taken); in configs/curation-routes.yaml

M3Score each content filter's drops on its own target and on bad textanalysis.py::precision_rows

Input

A judged sample of documents, each with its source, the filters that kept or dropped it, and one judge verdict. A verdict gives the language, a coherence score from 1 to 5, a text type such as prose, boilerplate or garbage, and an adult-or-spam flag.

Output

One row per filter, pooled over sources and then per source, with the target precision and the drop precision at the lenient bar. Each rate carries its Wilson interval and its call against the record's bars ([D2]). Written to tables/audit-precision-by-filter-and-source.csv for the earlier audit's sample.

How

Each filter is scored only on the documents it dropped.

  1. Keep the documents from the 18 selected sources that a content filter dropped and the judge read. A document dropped by one filter counts only for that filter.
  2. Mark a drop as on target by the filter's own test ([D1]). Language: the judge does not call it Slovene. Spam: flagged adult or spam. Quality: coherence 2 or lower, or garbage. Repetition: boilerplate or garbage.
  3. Mark a drop as bad text when it has coherence 2 or lower, is garbage or boilerplate, or is flagged adult or spam. The language filter is not scored on bad text.
  4. For a filter and a group of drops, compute the precision p=h/n, where n is the number of judged drops in the group and h how many pass the test, with its 95% Wilson interval.
  5. Pool by concatenating every source's drops, so each source weighs by its judged drops, not by its volume.
  6. Call a rate "holds" at 0.6 or more, "fails" below 0.5, and "open" between. A source with fewer than 20 judged drops gets no call.
Code
analysis.py::precision_rows
Settings
none; the bars are the record's ([D2])

M4Re-apply a candidate's quality filter to the documents the earlier audit saw it dropanalysis.py::refilter_rows

Input

The documents from the 18 selected sources that the quality filter dropped in the earlier audit's judged sample, each with its judge verdict. One item is such a document, with its source.

Output

Per source, per route and pooled, how many of those documents the candidate's quality filter now keeps, and the share of them that is bad text. Beside it, the target and bad-text precision of the ones it still drops ([M3]). Written to tables/curation-routes-audit-quality-refilter-by-route-and-source.csv for the candidate-routes build.

How

The judge read only each document's opening, so the filter is re-applied to the full text.

  1. Read each document's full text from the candidate build's input to the quality filter, matching the opening the judge read. A document is counted once even when the sample lists it twice, so a source can show fewer documents here than drops in the earlier audit's scoring ([M3]).
  2. Leave out, and count apart, two kinds of document. One is absent from that input, because an earlier filter of the candidate build drops it or because its source's document ids changed since the audit's build. The other is present only with text that no longer starts with the judged opening, so its verdict does not describe it.
  3. Build each source's quality filter with its route's settings and its own on top ([M1]), including the repaired letter rule ([M2]).
  4. Run the filter on each document. A kept document is rescued; the rest are the candidate filter's drops.
  5. Over the rescued documents, compute the share judged bad text, b=rbad/r, where r is the number rescued and rbad how many of them are bad text, with its 95% Wilson interval.
  6. Score the documents still dropped on the quality target and on bad text, as for the earlier audit's drops ([M3]). A group with fewer than 20 still dropped gets no call.
Code
analysis.py::refilter_rows
Settings
none; the filter settings are the candidate's, in configs/curation-routes.yaml

M5List every quality rule each still-dropped document failsanalysis.py::drop_rule_rows

Input

The documents the candidate's quality filter still drops in [M4], each with its judge verdict. One item is such a document, with its source and route.

Output

Per route, source and set of failed rules, the first rule failed, how many documents fail exactly that set, and how many of them the judge found to be the quality target or bad text. Each rule is named by the setting that steers it; one setting, the symbol ratio, caps the hash marks and the ellipses per word, so it steers two rules. The rule on lines ending in an ellipsis is a separate setting. Written to tables/curation-routes-audit-quality-drops-by-rule-and-source.csv.

How

The quality filter stops at the first rule a document fails, so a document that fails two rules would still be dropped if only the first were loosened.

  1. Run the source's quality filter on the document and note the rule it fails.
  2. Switch that rule off, by setting it to 0 on a copy of the filter, and run it again; repeat until the document is kept.
  3. Group the documents by the set of rules they failed. A set of one rule counts the documents that switching that rule off alone would keep; loosening it only part of the way may keep fewer.
Code
analysis.py::drop_rule_rows
Settings
none; the filter settings are the candidate's, in configs/curation-routes.yaml

M6Trace the medical source's exact-dedup drops to where their copies come fromanalysis.py::copy_origin_rows

Input

The medical source's documents that reach exact dedup in the candidate build, each with the text id its release gives it. Beside them, which of them exact dedup keeps and which reach the finished corpus, the output of sentence dedup. One item is such a document.

Output

One row per origin, with how many documents it holds, their share of the documents entering exact dedup, and how many reach the finished corpus. Written to tables/curation-routes-medical-exact-dedup-documents-by-copy-origin.csv.

How

Exact dedup keeps one document per distinct text, so each drop has a kept copy somewhere.

  1. Group the documents by their exact text.
  2. A group with no kept document was kept from another source; all its documents count as copies of another source.
  3. Otherwise, every document past the first under one text id is the same record held again; every further text id the text is filed under adds one drop under another text id.
  4. Among the kept documents, one past the first under its text id is a second text of one record. It differs from the first, so exact dedup cannot see it as a copy. In the finished corpus it counts only while its record still has another text there.
Code
analysis.py::copy_origin_rows
Settings
none; the source is fixed in the script

M7Read the judge's agreement with the person and call each clause on the fresh drawanalysis.py::agreement_rows

Input

One judge run over the fresh draw with the 116 hand-labelled documents spread through it ([D11]). One item is a document with its verdict, and for a hand-labelled document also the person's label on the same rubric.

Output

The judge's agreement with the person per test, the fresh draw's precision per filter and source ([M3]), and a call per hypothesis clause. Written to tables/curation-routes-fresh-judge-agreement-with-person-by-test.csv, tables/curation-routes-fresh-precision-by-filter-and-source.csv and tables/curation-routes-fresh-hypothesis-calls-by-clause.csv.

How

The gate and the findings read the same run ([D3]).

  1. Pair each hand-labelled document's label with the run's verdict on it; a labelled document without a verdict stops the reading.
  2. The tests are bad text at the lenient bar and each filter's target ([D1]). For each, turn both sides into yes-or-no calls and compute Cohen's κ, κ=(po−pe)/(1−pe), where po is the share of documents both call alike and pe the share chance would give from how often each says yes.
  3. The gate passes when κ on bad text at the lenient bar is at least 0.6. The other tests' κ show which verdict fields the person and the judge read alike.
  4. Score the fresh draw's drops as for the earlier audit's ([M3]). Hand-labelled documents the draw did not hold are left out.
  5. Call a clause confirmed when every rate it reads holds, refuted when any fails, and inconclusive otherwise. H1 to H4 read their filter's target precision; H5 reads bad-text precision on the spam, quality and repetition filters. A rate counts when it is pooled or its source has at least 20 judged drops. Every call carries whether the run passed the gate.
Code
analysis.py::agreement_rows, analysis.py::clause_rows
Settings
none; the gate and the bars are the record's ([D2], [D3])

M8Estimate how much bad text each filter removes and how much good text it loses on each sourceanalysis.py::trade_off_rows

Input

The candidate build's document counts per source after every stage, and the fresh draw's judged drops ([M7]). One item is a filter on a source.

Output

Per filter, a pooled row then one row per source. Each row holds the documents the filter drops in the whole build, how many of its drops were judged, the share of them estimated bad, the bad documents removed and the good documents lost. It also holds a call at the rate of one good document per bad one ([D12]) and whether the judge run passed the agreement gate ([D3]). For the language filter, "bad" in these columns means not Slovene. Written to tables/curation-routes-fresh-bad-removed-and-good-lost-by-filter-and-source.csv, most good text lost first within each filter.

How

The draw takes 40 drops per filter and source whatever the source's size, so its shares are scaled back to each source's volume.

  1. The documents a filter drops on a source, d, are its count before the filter minus its count after.
  2. The bad share s is the share of the source's judged drops that are bad text at the lenient bar; for the language filter it is the share the judge does not call Slovene ([D1]).
  3. Bad removed is d·s, rounded to a whole document; good lost is d minus bad removed.
  4. The pooled row sums d over the sources with judged drops, and its share weighs each source by its drops, spool=∑idisi/∑idi, where i runs over those sources. A source the draw sampled no drops from is left out of both.
  5. Call a source "keep" when s≥0.5 and "switch off" below. A source with fewer than 20 judged drops gets no call, nor does the pooled row, since the setting is chosen per source.
Code
analysis.py::trade_off_rows
Settings
none; the exchange rate is the record's ([D12])

M9Split each source's quality and repetition drops by the rules they fail, on both judged samplesanalysis.py::rule_trade_off_rows

Input

The judged documents the quality or repetition filter dropped, in the earlier audit's sample and in the fresh draw, from the 18 selected sources ([D13]). One item is such a document with its verdict; a document judged in both keeps its fresh verdict.

Output

One row per filter, source and set of failed rules. It holds how many judged documents fail exactly that set, how many of them come from the fresh draw, and their bad-text share. It also holds the documents, bad documents removed and good documents lost that set stands for in the candidate build, and whether the fresh judge run passed the agreement gate ([D3]). Every set is listed, most good text lost first within each filter; which rules to loosen is decided from it in the next step, so no row carries a call. Written to tables/curation-routes-judged-bad-removed-and-good-lost-by-rule-and-source.csv.

How

The rules are read on the full text under the candidate's settings, so both samples describe the same build.

  1. Read each document's full text from the candidate build's input to the filter, as for the quality re-score ([M4]); documents absent there, or present with other text, are left out.
  2. Build each source's filter with its route's settings and its own ([M1]).
  3. List every rule the document fails, as for the quality rules ([M5]), each named by the setting that steers it. The repetition filter's line and paragraph limits are switched off one at a time. Each of its two n-gram families, the most frequent 2- to 4-word phrase and the repeated 5- to 10-word phrases, is switched off whole. A document the candidate filter keeps is left out: it is not one of its drops.
  4. For a source, let n be its judged documents still dropped and d the documents the filter drops there in the build ([M8]). A set failed by k of them, b of which are bad text, stands for d·k/n documents, of which d·b/n are bad removed, each rounded to a whole document, and the rest good lost.
  5. The earlier audit's documents were drawn from its own build's drops; those the candidate still drops count as a sample of the candidate's drops, weighing the same as fresh ones.
Code
analysis.py::rule_trade_off_rows, analysis.py::failing_rules
Settings
none; the filter settings are the candidate's, in configs/curation-routes.yaml

M10Estimate the good and bad text each route's setting changes would keepanalysis.py::read_setting_changes

Input

The judged quality and repetition drops of both samples with their full text and verdicts, as for the rule breakdown ([M9]), and a list of setting changes per route. One item is a judged document the candidate build drops.

Output

Per route and variant, a pooled row then one row per source. A variant is one change alone or, on a route with several, all its changes together. Each row holds the judged drops, how many of them the variant keeps, the documents it would keep in the build, their bad share, and how many are bad and good. It also holds a call at the rate of one good document per bad one ([D12]) and whether the fresh judge run passed the agreement gate ([D3]). Written to tables/tuning-filter-settings-good-and-bad-kept-by-change-and-source.csv, most good text gained first within each variant.

How

Each change is tried on the documents the candidate build drops, so only what it would rescue is counted.

  1. Merge the change's settings over each source's own ([M1]) and build its quality and repetition filters.
  2. A judged drop is rescued when the variant's filter at that stage keeps it. A quality drop must also pass the variant's repetition filter, the next one it meets. Exact and sentence dedup are not run, so some rescued documents would still be removed there.
  3. Scale as in the rule breakdown. Let n be the judged drops at a filter on a source, d the documents dropped there in the build, and k of the n rescued, b of them bad. The variant keeps d·k/n documents, of which d·b/n are bad, each rounded to a whole document. A source's two filters are summed.
  4. The pooled row sums a route's sources. It is called "adopt" when under half of what it keeps is bad and at least 20 judged drops are rescued, and "reject" otherwise ([D16]); source rows carry no call. The 20 are counted over the route, so a large source may rest on a few of them.
Code
analysis.py::read_setting_changes, analysis.py::rescue_outcomes, analysis.py::setting_change_rows
Settings
changes (the setting changes tried on each route), stage (the filter a change loosens), settings (the knobs merged over the route's; 0 switches a quality rule off, an empty n-gram list a repetition family); in configs/tuning-filter-settings.yaml

M11Measure the good and bad text the loosened build gained, beside the estimateanalysis.py::gain_rows

Input

The frozen build ([D10]) and the loosened build ([D16]), with document counts per source and stage. Each comes with a judged draw of its quality and repetition drops: the fresh draw for the frozen build, the third draw for the loosened one ([D13]). One item is a judged document one build drops at one of the two filters.

Output

Per route, a pooled row then one row per source, most good text gained first. Each row holds the documents gained, bad and good text gained, a 95% interval on bad text gained, and the per-route estimate made before the build ([M10]). Written to tables/curation-routes-loosened-good-and-bad-gained-by-route-and-source.csv, beside the third run's agreement with the person (tables/curation-routes-loosened-judge-agreement-with-person-by-test.csv) and the loosened build's remaining drops scored as in [M8] (tables/curation-routes-loosened-bad-removed-and-good-lost-by-filter-and-source.csv).

How

Both builds feed the same documents into the quality filter. So what the loosened build gains before dedup is what the frozen build's two filters drop minus what the loosened build's drop.

  1. Each source must enter the quality filter with the same count in both builds, or the reading stops.
  2. A filter its route leaves unchanged must drop the same count in both builds, or the reading stops; it adds nothing and is skipped.
  3. For a changed filter, with d documents dropped in a build and b of its n judged drops bad, it drops d·b/n bad documents. Gains are frozen minus loosened, for documents and for bad text; good text is the rest. A repetition term can be negative, since the loosened build feeds that filter more documents.
  4. The interval on bad text is ±1.96V, with V=∑d2p~(1−p~)/n over every estimated filter of both builds. Here p~=(b+1.92)/(n+3.84), the Agresti–Coull share, so a share of 0 or 1 still counts as uncertain.
  5. Nothing is cut at zero, so a source can show negative bad text by chance; pooled rows sum such noise out.
  6. The estimate beside a route is the variant applying all its changes ([M10]). Estimate and measurement share the frozen build's fresh-draw shares, so their agreement checks only the loosened build's counts and the third draw's shares.
Code
analysis.py::gain_rows
Settings
configs/tuning-filter-settings.yaml names the filters each route changes; the bad-text bar is [D1]'s lenient bar

M12Measure the share of bad text each build keeps, weighted by volume, against the baseline'sanalysis.py::judged_kept

Input

Three builds, the baseline rebuild ([D5]), the frozen build ([D10]) and the loosened build ([D16]). Each comes with its document count per source after the repetition filter and judge verdicts on a draw of the documents it kept there. The baseline's draw is the earlier audit's, taken from that audit's build, which ran at the same settings except the spam repair and the five doubled sources; its per-source shares stand in for the rebuild's. The frozen build's draw is the fresh draw and the loosened build's the third draw ([D13]). One item is a judged document a build kept at the repetition filter.

Output

Per build, a volume-weighted row and then one row per source, each with the documents kept, how many were judged, the residual bad rate with its 95% interval, and the good documents kept. Beside it, one row per build other than the baseline: the rise of its weighted rate above the baseline's with a 95% interval, and the good documents it keeps beyond the baseline's. That row also carries the answer to the amended question ([D17]) and whether the build's judge run passed the agreement gate ([D3]). Written to tables/residual-bad-rate-by-build-and-source.csv and tables/residual-bad-rate-rise-by-build.csv.

How

The repetition filter is the last stage all three draws sample, so "kept" means its output and the dedup stages are not counted.

  1. For a build and a source, let k be the documents kept at the repetition filter, n the judged documents drawn as kept there, and b how many of them are bad text at the lenient bar. The build keeps k·b/n bad documents on that source; the rest are good. A source that keeps documents but has no judged kept one stops the reading.
  2. A source's rate is b/n with its 95% Wilson interval.
  3. The volume-weighted rate is the bad documents summed over sources divided by the kept documents summed over sources, so each source weighs by what it keeps, not by how many of its documents were judged. Its 95% interval is ±1.96V/∑k, with V=∑k2p~(1−p~)/n over sources and p~ the Agresti–Coull share, as for the gains ([M11]).
  4. A build's rise is its weighted rate minus the baseline's. The interval on the rise adds the two builds' variances, since their draws are independent.
  5. Good documents kept beyond the baseline's are the build's good documents minus the baseline's. The answer to the amended question is yes when that is positive and the low end of the rise's interval is at most two points ([D17]).
Code
analysis.py::judged_kept, analysis.py::residual_rows, analysis.py::residual_rise_rows
Settings
none; the bar is the record's ([D17]), and the kept stage is fixed in the script as the repetition filter

Decisions

D1Judge each filter on what it is built to catch, and the content filters also on bad text2026-10-05

Decision

Each content filter has its own target. Language: the judge says the text is not Slovene. Spam: the judge flags it adult or spam. Quality: coherence 2 or lower, or garbage. Repetition: boilerplate or garbage. The spam, quality and repetition filters are also scored on bad text at the lenient bar. The language filter is not.

Why

Whether a text is Slovene says nothing about its quality, so the language filter cannot be expected to drop bad text. The earlier audit's bar counted non-Slovene drops as bad text, mixing the two.

Alternatives
  • The earlier audit's single bar for every filter: it blends a filter's purpose with general quality, and hides which one fails.
History
2026-10-05 first version, at record creation

D2Count a filter as working at 0.6, and as failing below 0.52026-10-05

Decision

A clause is confirmed at a rate of at least 0.6, pooled and on every source with at least 20 judged drops. It is refuted below 0.5 on any of them.

Why

0.6 is the line below which the earlier audit called a filter wrong, and the earlier filters sat far below it. 0.8 would likely fail on the spam filter over web crawls even if routing fixes the curated sources.

Alternatives
  • 0.8, the earlier audit's confirm bar: too ambitious for the spam filter on web crawls.
History
2026-10-05 first version, at record creation

D3Tune on the old evidence, claim only on a fresh draw2026-10-19

Decision

Thresholds are tuned on the earlier audit's judge verdicts and 116 hand labels. Every claim rests on a fresh draw under a new seed, judged only after the thresholds freeze. The agreement gate is read on the judge run the findings use. No second judge from another model family is run.

Why

Thresholds fitted to one judge's verdicts on one sample stop being neutral evidence. The earlier audit read its gate on one run and its findings on another, which weakened every number it reported.

History
2026-10-19 second judge dropped at the project lead's call: a run costs too much for what it would add, since the judged draws already show the dataset's quality; retitled from "… read by two judges"

D4Keep the corpus above the volume targets while tuning2026-10-05

Decision

No setting may push the final corpus below KPI 3, more than 5B estimated tokens, or medicine or science below KPI 4, more than 500k estimated tokens each. Domains are read from source labels. Document-level domain counts from the planned KPI coverage experiment are added beside them once that classifier exists.

Why

Tuning trades kept text against quality, and the project's corpus-size targets bound that trade. Source labels already cover the curated domain sources, so this experiment need not wait for the classifier.

History
2026-10-05 first version, from the ordering agreed with the KPI coverage experiment

D5Take the baseline from a fresh build of the shared corpus at main's settings2026-10-05

Decision

The baseline is the shared corpus rebuilt with the pipeline as it stands on main: the repaired spam filter, the current source list, and no per-source routes. The repaired spam filter counts each spam term once, however often it repeats. It is not the earlier audit's build.

Why

The earlier build counted five sources twice and predates the spam repair. Two sources are now skipped as copies of others: parlamint_si inside siparl, legal_mc4 inside c4. Main's settings are no setting of this experiment, so they rebuild the shared corpus.

History
2026-10-05 first version, after every unit of the on-disk corpus was found out of date

D6Score every candidate setting on a full build of the pipeline2026-10-05

Decision

Each candidate route and threshold set is a full pipeline build, written into this experiment's own data folder and never over the shared corpus.

Why

Dedup across the corpus and the volume targets ([D4]) depend on what every source keeps. Only a full build shows both, so the whole pipeline runs for each candidate.

Alternatives
  • Rerun only the filters on the earlier audit's judged documents: fast, but blind to dedup and to corpus totals.
History
2026-10-05 first version, at the project lead's call

D7Switch the language and spam filters off on curated sources2026-10-08

Decision

The curated-prose route runs neither the language nor the spam filter, except that the crawl of PDF documents keeps its language filter. The medical-and-academic route runs no spam filter but keeps the language filter. These sources leave the H1 and H2 clauses for filters they skip ([M1]).

Why

In the earlier audit, none of the 40 judged language drops on any of the six edited-prose sources was judged not Slovene. At most one of 40 spam drops on any curated source was spam ([M3]). These sources are edited Slovene text, so the filters there remove only usable prose.

Alternatives
  • Keep both filters and raise their thresholds: the wrong language drops are confident calls (Romanian, Dutch, Czech for Slovene), so no confidence threshold separates them.
History
2026-10-08 the PDF crawl joins the curated-prose route with its language filter on: in the earlier audit none of its 40 judged spam drops was spam, and 0.375 of its language drops were not Slovene, against none on the other curated sources, so its language filter still removes real foreign text

D8Repair the quality filter's letter rule rather than lower its floor2026-10-12

Decision

On every route, the quality filter's rule that most words contain a letter counts only tokens that are not punctuation marks, at the Gopher floor of 0.8 ([M2]).

Why

Datatrove splits each punctuation mark into its own word, so comma-dense prose fails a rule meant for numbers and symbols. In the earlier audit's sample, this rule caused most quality drops on nearly every source. With punctuation set aside, those dropped documents had a median letter share of 0.87 to 1.00.

Alternatives
  • Lower the floor per route, to 0.65: the floor would then track how much punctuation a source uses, not how much junk it holds.
  • Raise the floor on the raw crawls to drop the junk the repair keeps: that junk has the same letter share as good text.
History
2026-10-12 raw crawls keep the floor at 0.8, at the project lead's call: about one in six audit drops the repair keeps there is junk ([M4]), but no letter floor, stopword share or line measure tested drops it without as much good text

D9Loosen the curated-prose quality filter only where its drops were usable text2026-10-16

Decision

On the curated-prose route, the letter floor drops from 0.8 to 0.55, and the news source skips the rule on lines ending in an ellipsis. The 20-word floor and the stopword rule, first kept, were loosened on the judged samples ([D16]).

Why

The repaired filter still drops 106 of the audit's judged documents here ([M5]). Of these, 39 news teasers fail the ellipsis rule and 16 tables and listings fail the letter rule first. The judge found none of them broken text. Short parliament turns and listings without stopwords stayed dropped until the judged samples showed them mostly good ([D16]).

Alternatives
  • Switch the quality filter off on curated prose: it would also keep the number-only PDF tables, at letter shares near 0.2.
  • Lower the 20-word floor for the parliament source alone: the judged samples later favoured lowering it route-wide ([D16]).
History
2026-10-16 the 20-word floor lowered to 10 and the stopword rule switched off on this route ([D16])

D10Freeze the thresholds of the second candidate build and draw the fresh sample from it2026-10-14

Decision

The thresholds freeze as configs/curation-routes.yaml stands at commit 4425f23, the settings of the second candidate build. The fresh draw comes from that build with the earlier audit's sampler settings, 40 documents per source, stage and decision at every stage, under the new seed 20261014.

Why

That build already ran at exactly the frozen settings, so a rebuild would reproduce it ([D6], a full build per candidate setting). Keeping every sampler setting but the seed keeps the fresh verdicts comparable with the earlier audit's, stage by stage, while no document choice rests on the tuning evidence ([D3]).

Alternatives
  • Sample only the four content filters: about a third less judging, but no fresh reading of the dedup stages beside the audit's.
  • Wait for the medical extraction fix first: it changes one source and its fix lies outside this experiment.
History
2026-10-14 first version, at the project lead's call

D11Judge the fresh draw with the earlier audit's judge, the 116 hand-labelled documents in the same run2026-10-19

Decision

Sonnet 5 judges the fresh draw on the earlier rubric, in groups of 10, as in the earlier audit. The 116 documents the person labelled are spread evenly through the draw, so each is judged in the run the findings use. They keep their ids, so nothing marks them to the judge.

Why

The same judge keeps the fresh verdicts comparable with the tuning evidence, so only the thresholds change between the two readings. Reading the agreement gate on this very run avoids the earlier audit's split between a calibration run and a findings run.

Alternatives
  • Sonnet 5.5: possibly closer to the person, but the judge would change along with the thresholds.
  • Opus 5.5: the strongest model, slowest and heaviest on quota, with the same confound.
  • Judge the 116 documents in a run of their own: the gate would again read on a run the findings do not use.
History
2026-10-19 the 116 documents also spread through the third draw ([D13]), at the project lead's call

D12Keep a filter on a source only where at least half of what it drops is bad text2026-10-15

Decision

One good document lost weighs as much as one bad document removed. A filter, or one of its rules, stays on a source when at least half of the documents it drops there are bad text at the lenient bar, estimated over the source's whole volume.

Why

The fresh draw shows the filters trading good text for bad at very different rates per source. Settings need one exchange rate to be chosen against, and 1:1 is neutral between corpus size and cleanliness. It matches the record's refute line of 0.5 ([D2]).

Alternatives
  • Two good documents per bad one removed: a cleaner corpus at a large loss of usable text.
  • One good document per two bad ones: favours volume, keeps more spam.
History
2026-10-15 first version, at the project lead's call

D13Retune on both judged samples, check on a third draw limited to what changed2026-10-16

Decision

The next settings are tuned on the earlier audit's and the fresh draw's verdicts together. The fresh draw thereby becomes tuning evidence. A third draw under a new seed then checks the result, limited to the filters and sources whose settings change.

Why

The fresh draw is the best evidence on the frozen settings, and it shows where they lose good text. Keeping it held back would tune on the older, less informative sample. A third draw restores a check that no setting was tuned on ([D3]).

Alternatives
  • Tune on the earlier audit's sample only and keep the fresh draw for checking: clean, but tunes on evidence the fresh draw showed to mislead.
History
2026-10-16 the loosened settings ([D16]) build into their own folder, so the frozen second build stays for comparison, at the project lead's call

D14Leave a learned quality classifier to a follow-up experiment2026-10-15

Decision

This experiment changes only which filters and rules run on each source, and their thresholds. A classifier trained on the judge's verdicts, to catch the spam and boilerplate the rules cannot separate from good text, is left to an experiment of its own.

Why

A classifier changes the pipeline's design and needs its own hypothesis, training data and evaluation. The rule settings can be fixed with the evidence already judged.

History
2026-10-15 first version, at the project lead's call

D15Keep the Slovenian slices of the multilingual collections in the corpus2026-10-15

Decision

Fineweb2, culturax and finepdf stay in the corpus; their bad text is handled by per-source filter settings like any other source.

Why

They are the Slovenian slices of multilingual collections: the language filter drops under 1% of each. Exact and sentence dedup already remove what they share with other sources, and what remains is about 36% of the finished corpus's words, with bad-text shares within the other web crawls' range.

Alternatives
  • Drop fineweb2 and culturax: loses about 24% of the words, mostly unique web text.
  • Drop all three: loses about 36% of the words, including PDF text no other source holds.
History
2026-10-15 first version, at the project lead's call

D16Loosen the filters per route, judged on each route's pooled drops2026-10-16

Decision

The changes tried are set per route. On web crawls, the ellipsis-line rule and the repeated-phrase rule go off. On curated prose, the 20-word floor drops to 10, and the stopword rule and the repetition filter go off. On medical and academic text, the repetition filter goes off. Each route is called on its sources' drops pooled ([M10]).

Why

Tried one at a time, each change kept more good text than bad on its route. Most sources have fewer than 20 rescued judged drops, too few for a call of their own, and routes already group sources by text type ([M1]). The fresh judge run failed the agreement gate, so the calls hold only until the third draw ([D13]).

Alternatives
  • Repetition filter off on every route: a scratch estimate trying each change alone kept about 0.5M more bad web documents, mostly c4 and cc100.
  • Only the repeated-phrase rule off everywhere: keeps the repetition filter on where almost nothing it drops is bad.
  • Call each source on its own figure: unsteady below 20 judged drops.
History
2026-10-16 the project lead kept the three quality-rule changes (ellipsis-line rule, 20-word floor, stopword rule) beside the repetition changes

D17Also ask whether the loosened build keeps more good text without a dirtier kept corpus2026-10-20

Decision

Beside the clauses, the record asks whether the loosened build keeps more good text than the baseline, with a volume-weighted residual bad rate at most 2 points above the baseline's. Rates come from judged kept documents, the baseline's from the earlier audit's draw ([M12]). The answer is yes unless the whole 95% interval on the rise lies above 2 points.

Why

No clause can be called, since every judge run sits below the agreement gate ([F9]). Curation also aims at a larger, no dirtier corpus, which the clauses do not score. Forty judged kept documents per source leave the interval about ten points wide, so the bar reads its low end. A no then needs a rise of about seven points.

Alternatives
  • Also cap each source's rise at 5 points: within the noise of about 40 judged kept documents per source.
  • No bar, only the rates reported: leaves the amended question without an answer.
  • Answer from the point estimate alone: claims more than the draws can separate.
  • Call it inconclusive while the interval spans the bar: leaves the amended question open at this sample size.
History
2026-10-20 the bar is read against the interval's low end, at the project lead's call, after the loosened build's point estimate was seen above it; the frozen build's rise corrected from about one point to about two, measured from the saved draws

Whether the Sloleks 3.2 stem-ending split ranks Slovene tokenizers as the lemma-alignment gold does

in Slovene tokenizer choiceuses Byte-level BPE, Character BPE, WordPiece, Unigram, MorphBPE, MorphPieceMLflow #16PR #33concluded 2026-10-25
Hypothesis
The tokenizers rank the same on morpheme-boundary F1 whether the gold is the project's lemma-alignment heuristic, with its word-class tags corrected, or the stem-ending split that the Sloleks 3.2 authors released. Scoring on the manually checked forms alone gives the same ranking as scoring on all forms.
partial
Needs
PeopleNone.
ComputeLocal CPU, four workers at most. One streaming pass over the corpus fixes the split and its statistics. Five algorithms train in minutes to an hour at 64k. MorphBPE's single-threaded merge loop took 31 hours at 128k, which bounds the sweep: all 24 tokenizers trained in 31 hours on four workers.
Data accessSloleks 3.2 is an unreleased file the lexicon's author shared directly; it is cited as Sloleks 3.1 (hdl.handle.net/11356/2080), as the author asked.
External dependencyNone.
Clause mixedClaimHolds ifFails ifResult

confirmed F1 The two golds rank the tokenizers with a Kendall's τ of 0.86, and the whole bootstrap interval sits above the 0.8 bar.

Findings

F1The heuristic gold and the Sloleks gold rank the tokenizers alikekey · H1

Summary

The two golds rank the tokenizers with a Kendall's τ of 0.86, and the whole bootstrap interval sits above the 0.8 bar.

Reading
  • Both golds put the same algorithms at the top and the same at the bottom. Under either gold Unigram ranks above MorphBPE, which ranks above WordPiece, and a gap separates those three from character BPE, BPE and MorphPiece. The disagreement sits inside an algorithm, where its four vocabulary sizes swap places. On the tokenizers that train without a morpheme table the agreement rises to 0.95. The frequency-weighted and the multi-token readings agree with the main one, while the manual-only reading and the forms with an ending have intervals that cross the bar.
  • The claim that the two golds rank the tokenizers alike ([H1]) is confirmed, since τ and its whole interval lie above the bar of 0.8. The corrected heuristic places its cut differently from the authors' split on many forms, yet which tokenizer looks morphologically best does not depend on that placement.
  • A vocabulary-size order that reversed between the golds inside one algorithm would overturn the reading. The scatter shows each algorithm's four points moving along the diagonal, so the gold shifts a score without reordering the family.
Implication

The tokenizer sweep of June 2026, written up in docs/notes/, rests on the uncorrected gold, whose ranking agrees with the Sloleks one at only τ 0.64. The later experiments score on the Sloleks gold and reread the June comparisons on it.

runs73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee (the sweep's parent run, 24 child runs), scored by analysis.py at 8f408e8 on the scored-form golds

history2026-10-25 first result, run 73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee, analysis commit 8f408e8.

F2The manually checked forms rank the tokenizers differently from all formskey · H2

Summary

Ranking the tokenizers on the manually checked forms alone agrees with the all-forms ranking at τ 0.69, below the 0.9 bar.

Reading
  • On the manual forms MorphBPE overtakes Unigram at every size but the largest, and the algorithms that train without a morpheme table score higher with smaller vocabularies. On all forms Unigram leads from 32k upwards and BPE, character BPE and MorphPiece improve as the vocabulary grows. On the manual forms their order by size reverses, so a larger vocabulary scores lower on the forms the lexicon's authors checked.
  • The claim that the manual slice ranks the tokenizers as all forms do ([H2]) is refuted, since the whole interval ends below the bar of 0.9. By the verdict rule this is the automatic-rows reading: the golds agree, but the morph score is reported on the manual forms first.
  • A manual slice drawn at random from all forms would have to agree with them, and only noise could then separate the rankings. The slice is not random: its word-class mix differs from the whole, which is where the disagreement comes from ([F4]).
Implication

Every morph score of the later tokenizer experiments is reported on the manually checked forms first, with the all-forms score beside it, since the automatic rows move the ranking.

runs73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee, scored by analysis.py at 8f408e8 on the scored-form golds

history2026-10-25 first result, run 73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee, analysis commit 8f408e8.

F4The manual slice reorders the tokenizers through its word-class mixsupporting F2

Summary

Within a word class the manual and the all-forms rankings agree at τ above 0.9 for adjectives and verbs, but the classes disagree.

Reading
  • The disagreement lies between word classes, not between the checked and the unchecked rows of one class. The manual and the all-forms rankings agree for adjectives and verbs and less for nouns, where τ is 0.74. The verbs alone rank the tokenizers far from the all-forms order, τ 0.41, so the pooled ranking is mostly the nouns' ranking.
  • For the manual slice's disagreement with all forms ([F2]) this means the slice disagrees because nouns are nearly three quarters of all scored forms but under half of the manual ones. The all-forms ranking follows the nouns, and the manual ranking gives adjectives and verbs more weight.
  • A within-class agreement as low as the cross-slice one would overturn the reading, since the automatic rows themselves would then move the ranking. Nouns come closest, so an audit of the automatic noun rows is the one check left.
Implication

A later gold reports the morph score per word class beside the pooled one, since the pooled ranking follows the class mix of whichever slice is scored.

runs73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee, scored by analysis.py at 8f408e8 on the scored-form golds

history2026-10-25 first result, run 73b5a885e4bf4f2994b285573dab10ee, analysis commit 8f408e8.

F3On all forms only Unigram's morpheme-boundary F1 still rises at the largest vocabulary, while compression and Morph-Edit-Distance keep improving for every algorithmkey

Summary

From 64k to 128k every algorithm still gains on fertility and Morph-Edit-Distance, but on all forms morpheme-boundary F1 rises for Unigram alone.

Reading
  • Compression and edit distance have not levelled off for any algorithm, and Rényi efficiency falls at every step. Over the last size step, fertility and compression still gain half to three quarters of what they gained over the first, for all six algorithms. Morph-Edit-Distance gains as much over the last step as over the first. Rényi efficiency, how evenly the tokens are used, falls at every step, which the rule records as no early gain. Morpheme-boundary F1 rises at the largest size for Unigram on both slices and for WordPiece on the manual forms only. On all forms it falls for WordPiece, character BPE and MorphBPE and barely moves for the rest. Each reading is in sweep-levelling-by-algorithm.csv.
  • The question which metrics still improve as the vocabulary grows ([Q1]) is partial: compression and Morph-Edit-Distance improve for every algorithm on both slices, but the other two morph metrics do not read alike. Morpheme-boundary F1 or Morph-Consistency reads differently on the manual and the all-forms score for every algorithm but Unigram. The compression answer is robust; the morph answer holds for Unigram only.
  • A larger vocabulary that bent Unigram's curve down, or a band rule in place of the quarter rule, would overturn the reading. A band rule reads a change narrower than its bootstrap interval as flat. The other algorithms' changes at the largest size are that narrow, so a band would call them flat, not falls.
Implication

The later tokenizer experiments keep 128k in the sweep for Unigram and for compression, and read a morpheme-boundary F1 change narrower than its interval as flat rather than by the quarter rule.

F5The vocabularies trained with a morpheme table carry the most rarely used tokensminor

Summary

At the largest vocabulary, tokens seen fewer than ten times in the training sample are about 1% of BPE's vocabulary and 27% of MorphPiece's.

Reading

A vocabulary trained on a morpheme table spends tokens on morphemes the corpus rarely uses, and a small model learns little for those embeddings, so this share ([D12]) weighs against MorphBPE and MorphPiece.

The alphabet cap that keeps the character-level vocabularies from filling up with single characters ([D14]) changes neither τ nor the order of the tokenizers, so it stays in the later sweeps.
